positiveFlows.title: ** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** IN THE UNITED STATES, FORESTS HAVE RECENTLY GAINED ATTENTION IN SCIENCE AND POLICY ARENAS AS TOOL FOR OFFSETTING CARBON EMISSIONS ARISING FROM OTHER INDUSTRIES. WITH AN UNCERTAIN CLIMATE FUTURE, HOWEVER, FORESTS ACROSS THE WEST ARE EXPECTED TO FACE MULTIPLE STRESSORS, INCLUDING PROLONGED DROUGHTS, FOREST HEALTH AND WILDFIRE - THE LATTER FUELED BY THE FIRST TWO. FURTHERMORE, WE KNOW LITTLE ABOUT THE LONGER-TERM IMPLICATIONS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT FOR FOREST RESILIENCY: WHICH TYPES OF FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ARE MOST EFFECTIVE IN CREATING A RESILIENCY RESPONSE IN MANAGED FORESTS. IN RESPONSE, THE PRINCIPAL AIM OF THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH PROJECT IS TO ASSESS THE POTENTIAL FOR IMPROVED FOREST MANAGEMENT TO CONTRIBUTE TO INCREASING AND SUSTAINING CARBON STOCKS IN THE WORKING FORESTS OF THE WEST. SPECIFICALLY, THIS PROJECT SETS OUT TO UNDERSTAND THE EFFECTS OF SPECIFIC FOREST MANAGEMENT ACTIONS ON FOREST CARBON ON FORESTLAND (INCL. TIMBERLAND) IN CALIFORNIA. TO THAT END, THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH PLANS TO USE A COMBINATION OF EXISTING OBSERVATIONAL DATA, FIELD MEASUREMENTS, DATA ANALYSIS AND AVAILABLE MODELING TOOLS TO TEST FOREST MANAGEMENT OUTCOMES. THIS RESEARCH PROJECT WILL ADDRESS A CRITICAL GAP IN TRANSLATING CLIMATE ADAPTATION METHODS INTO PRACTICAL FOREST MANAGEMENT TO BE USED BY STAKEHOLDERS IN FORESTRY AND PROVIDE A POLICY ROADMAP FOR INTEGRATING CARBON MANAGEMENT INTO PRACTICAL FOREST MANAGEMENT. FINALLY, THE FINDINGS OF THIS STUDY WILL SERVE AS A FOUNDATION IN BUILDING A LARGER RESEARCH FRAMEWORK FOR ASSESSING THE POTENTIAL FOR SPECIFIC TYPES OF TARGETED FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO CONTRIBUTE TO MANAGING, PROTECTING, AND SUSTAINING RESOURCES IN MANAGED FORESTLANDS ACROSS CALIFORNIA.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** ABRAHAM BALDWIN AGRICULTURAL COLLEGE (ABAC) IS IN TIFTON, GEORGIA AND HAS A STUDENT BODY OF OVER 3,700 INDIVIDUALS. MOST OF THE STUDENTS ARE CONSIDERED UNDERSERVED BECAUSE THEY COME FROM RURAL AND IMPOVERISHED AREAS OF THE STATE, ARE FIRST GENERATION STUDENTS, OR MINORITY INDIVIDUALS. RURAL MIGRATION OF YOUNGER POPULATIONS HAS CAUSED AN ECONOMIC IMBALANCE THROUGHOUT COMMUNITIES IN THE SOUTH, AND THEY CAN LACK NEEDED SERVICES IN THESE AREAS DUE TO THEIR DECLINING NUMBERS AND REDUCTION OF SKILLED EMPLOYEES. SPECIFICALLY, RURAL VETERINARY MEDICINE IS FACING A NATIONAL SHORTAGE OF PRACTITIONERS SPECIALIZING IN FOOD ANIMAL MEDICINE. WITHOUT AN ADEQUATE SUPPLY OF VETERINARIANS CARING FOR THESE ANIMALS, THE SUPPLY CHAIN COULD BE NEGATIVELY IMPACTED. ABAC HAS A SIGNIFICANT RURAL STUDENT POPULATION PURSING DEGREES IN BIOLOGY AND ANIMAL SCIENCE AND HAS HAD PREVIOUS SUCCESS OF PROMOTING VETERINARY MEDICINE THROUGH THEIR ACCEPTANCE INTO VETERINARY COLLEGE. WE WOULD LIKE TO FURTHER THESE EFFORTS BY CONTINUING OUR EXISTING PARTNERSHIP WITH UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA-TIFTON VETERINARY DIAGNOSTIC AND INVESTIGATIONAL LABORATORY AND BUILDING NEW AND LASTING RELATIONSHIPS WITH LOCAL VETERINARIAN CLINICS, THE STATE VETERINARIAN'S OFFICE, THE GEORGIA VETERINARY MEDICAL ASSOCIATION, AND WHITE OAK PASTURES. WE WANT TO PROVIDE OPTIMAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR ABAC STUDENTS TO GAIN UNIQUE EXPERIENCES THAT WILL HELP THEM BE MORE EMPLOYABLE BY PRODUCING GRADUATES THAT CAN RETURN TO RURAL COMMUNITIES AND BRING THEIR SKILL SETS TO BETTER SERVE THOSE AREAS. EDUCATIONAL ATTAINMENT BY ABAC GRADUATES RETURNING TO RURAL COMMUNITIES THAT PARTICIPATE IN OPPORTUNITIES PRESENTED TO THEM THROUGH THE RELATIONSHIPS FORMED WITH THIS PROPOSAL CAN HELP IMPROVE RURAL AREAS.

** AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** FARMERS ARE ON THE FRONT LINES OF CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS LIKE DROUGHT AND WILDFIRE (ADAMS ET AL.2021). CLIMATE CHANGE THREATENS FARMER LIVELIHOODS AND HEALTH, ESPECIALLY MENTAL HEALTH (ADAMSET AL. 2021). CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS ON ECONOMIC SECURITY AND FARMER DECISION-MAKING MAYEXACERBATE FARMLAND ACCESS CHALLENGES AND LAND INSECURITY, CONSISTENTLY CITED BY FARMERS AS THEIRGREATEST CHALLENGE (AKOFF ET AL. 2022). LIMITED FARMLAND ACCESS, INSECURE TENURE, AND A RAPIDLYAGING FARMER POPULATION POSE SIGNIFICANT THREATS TO US FOOD SECURITY, RURAL ECONOMICDEVELOPMENT, AND THE ABILITY OF FARMLAND TO FOSTER BIODIVERSITY AND SEQUESTER CARBON (PETERSEN-ROCKNEY ET AL. 2021). THE CURRENT DISTRIBUTION OF FARMLAND OWNERSHIP IN THE US - IN WHICH WHITEPEOPLE OWN 98% OF FARMLAND AND 87% OF FARMERS ARE MALE - DRIVES RURAL ECONOMIC INEQUITIES ASLANDOWNERS BENEFIT FROM CAPITAL ACCUMULATION AND GENERATIONS OF WEALTH BUILDING (HORST ANDMARION 2019; SHOEMAKER 2021). THE GROWING FINANCIALIZATION OF FARMLAND THREATENS TOEXACERBATE THESE TRENDS BY CONCENTRATING FARMLAND IN THE HANDS OF ABSENTEE OWNERS AND CORPORATEACTORS (FAIRBAIRN 2020; ASHWOOD ET AL 2022). EXISTING RESEARCH SHOWS THAT SOCIALLYDISADVANTAGED FARMERS (INDIGENOUS, WOMEN, VETERAN, BEGINNING, AND FARMERS OF COLOR) ARE MORELIKELY TO FARM ON MARGINAL LAND WITH INSECURE TENURE, MAKING THEM ESPECIALLY VULNERABLE TOCLIMATE IMPACTS (PETERSEN-ROCKNEY ET AL. 2021). GROWING AND RAISING DIVERSIFIED FOOD CROPS, ANDOFTEN EXPERIENCING ENGAGEMENT BARRIERS WITH FORMAL AGRICULTURAL ADVISORY INSTITUTIONS, SOCIALLYDISADVANTAGED FARMERS ARE OFTEN UNABLE TO ACCESS RISK-BUFFERING TECHNOLOGIES (E.G. CAPITAL-INTENSIVE IRRIGATION SYSTEMS) OR SUPPORTS (E.G. CROP INSURANCE) (LIVERMAN 2015; MINKOFF-ZERN2019). THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE REMAIN AN UNDERSTUDIED CATALYST FOR FARMLAND TRANSITION,POTENTIALLY EXACERBATING INSECURITY, WHILE ALSO PRESENTING POTENTIAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR MOREEQUITABLE DISTRIBUTION AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF FARMLAND. GIVEN EXISTING INEQUALITIES AND GROWINGCLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS, THE QUESTION OF FARMLAND TRANSITION--HOW AGRICULTURAL LAND, AS WELL ASTHE KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND LABOR ESSENTIAL TO WORKING IT, WILL BE TRANSFERRED TO THE NEXTGENERATION--IS URGENT FOR THE FUTURE OF AMERICAN AGRICULTURE.OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO IMPROVE FARMLAND TRANSITION AND SUPPORT SECURE LAND TENURE THATFACILITATES THE ADOPTION OF CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION PRACTICES THAT BOLSTER RESILIENTCOMMUNITY ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF AMERICAN FARMERS. TO SUPPORT THISGOAL, THIS CONFERENCE PLANNING GRANT WILL ESTABLISH CONNECTIONS AND COLLABORATIONS AROUND THEWAYS THAT CLIMATE CHANGE IS IMPACTING FARMLAND TRANSITION, INCLUDING ACCESS AND TENURE, FORFARMERS AND RANCHERS IN THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST, BEGINNING IN MONTANA. THIS PROJECT HAS THESPECIFIC OBJECTIVES TO 1) UNDERSTAND THE NEEDS AND FOSTER RELATIONSHIPS WITH RURAL COMMUNITIESAND KEY STAKEHOLDERS IN THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST 2) CONVENE LEADING EXPERTS AND ASSESS EXISTINGKN,OWLEDGE ON THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN FARMLAND TRANSITION AND CLIMATE CHANGE IN ORDER TODEVELOP A COLLABORATIVE-LARGE-SCALE COMPREHENSIVE INITIATIVE 3) BUILD INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY ATTHE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA.OUR WORK FOCUSES ON THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST, A REGION LONG CHARACTERIZED BY THE IMPORTANCE OFFARMING AND RANCHING. MONTANA IS AN IDEAL PLACE TO BEGIN IDENTIFYING RESEARCH NEEDS, ANDEDUCATION AND EXTENSION OPPORTUNITIES, AT THE INTERSECTION OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND FARMLANDTRANSITION. A PREDOMINANTLY RURAL STATE WHERE MORE THAN 6.5% OF THE POPULATION IS INDIGENOUS AND12% OF THE POPULATION LIVES IN POVERTY, AGRICULTURE REMAINS AN IMPORTANT ECONOMIC AND CULTURALLIVELIHOOD (US CENSUS 2022). WITH 58.1 MILLION ACRES IN FARMS AND RANCHES, MONTANA RANKSSECOND IN THE NATION, BEHIND ONLY TEXAS, IN AGRICULTURAL LAND AREA (USDA NASS 2022). YETRECENT YEARS HAVE SEEN GROWING ECONOMIC DISPARITY, ESPECIALLY FOR THE STATE'S LARGE INDIGENOUSAND NATURAL RESOURCE DEPENDENT COMMUNITIES (SERCHEN ET AL. 2022; CAIRHE 2023). TODAY, THETWIN CRISES OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND LAND INSECURITY ARE UNFOLDING AGAINST THE BACKDROP OF OLDENVIRONMENTAL INJUSTICES - FROM SUPERFUND SITES TO INDIGENOUS LAND DISPOSSESSION. NEW CLIMATEFUTURES ARE BEING ACTIVELY CONTESTED IN THE LAW AND ON THE LAND, AS DEMONSTRATED BY THE RECENTHELD VS. MONTANA CASE, WHICH HIGHLIGHTS THE WAYS IN WHICH CLIMATE CHANGE IS ALREADY IMPACTINGRURAL LAND RELATIONS (FORBES 2023). MONTANA HAS BECOME HOME TO TWO DIVERGENT TRENDS THAT MAKEIT AN IDEAL PLACE FOR COMMUNITY-ENGAGED RESEARCH ON FARMLAND AND CLIMATE CHANGE: AN INCREASE ININVESTMENT FARMLAND PURCHASES BY NON-OPERATOR LANDLORDS (HAGGERTY ET AL. 2022), AND A ROBUSTFOOD SOVEREIGNTY MOVEMENT SUPPORTED BY A RICH LANDSCAPE OF INDIGENOUS AND FOOD JUSTICEORGANIZATIONS (MIFSI 2023). THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL ADDRESS A CRITICAL GAP BY EXAMINING HOWCLIMATE CHANGE, INCLUDING PHYSICAL AND POLICY IMPACTS, ARE SHIFTING FARMLAND ACCESS AND TENUREDYNAMICS.THIS PLANNING GRANT WILL LEAD TO AN INTEGRATED COLLABORATIVE-LARGE-SCALE COMPREHENSIVEINITIATIVE (TO BE SUBMITTED IN 2025) THAT WILL INVESTIGATE THE LAND-CLIMATE NEXUS ACROSS THEINTERMOUNTAIN WEST. IN DOING SO, THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY ADDRESSES NIFA RESEARCH NEED AREAS BYADVANCING THE BODY OF KNOWLEDGE WITHIN FOOD AND AGRICULTURE SCIENCES THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARYINQUIRY INTO THE CLIMATE-LAND NEXUS AND BY APPLYING THIS NEW KNOWLEDGE TO ADDRESS COMMUNITYAND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT ISSUES IN MONTANA AND SURROUNDING STATES THROUGH OUTREACH ANDEXTENSION WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, COMMUNITY, AND NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS. THROUGHOUTPLANNING AND IMPLEMENTATION STAGES, WE WILL ALSO ADDRESS EDUCATION NEED AREAS THROUGHCOLLABORATIVE INTERACTION WITH OTHER ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR FACULTYMEMBERS, AND EXPERIMENTAL LEARNING, INCLUDING GRADUATE RESEARCH ASSISTANTSHIPS AND CURRICULARDEVELOPMENT AT THE LAND-CLIMATE NEXUS THAT CAN PREPARE UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS FORCAREERS IN AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES. SPECIFIC,ALLY, THIS GRANT WILL FUND THREE IN-PERSON AND TWO VIRTUALLISTENING SESSIONS WITH FARMERS, RANCHERS, TRIBAL COMMUNITIES, AND POTENTIAL COMMUNITY PARTNERSAROUND THE STATE, A RESEARCH AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCE FOR ONE GRADUATE STUDENT,AND A SCHOLARLY CONFERENCE WITH ACADEMIC EXPERTS ON LAND AND CLIMATE CHANGE FROM ACROSS THEUS. TOGETHER, THESE PLANNING ACTIVITIES WILL HELP BUILD CAPACITY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA, ANON-LAND GRANT COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, IN AN UNDERFUNDED EPSCOR STATE WITH LARGE STUDENTPOPULATIONS FROM INDIGENOUS AND AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES.

negativeFlows.title: THE GOAL OF THIS LARGE-SCALE, COLLABORATIVE PROJECT IS CAPACITY BUILDING FOR THE ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY (A-STATE) COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE TO PARTICIPATE IN HIGH QUALITY RESEARCH AND EXTENSION. A-STATE'S COLLABORATIONS WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS-CENTER FOR ADVANCED SPATIAL TECHNOLOGY (UA-CAST), UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS SYSTEM DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE (UAEX), MIAMI UNIVERSITY (MU), AND UNIVERSITY OF DELAWARE (UD) WILL RAISE THE POTENTIAL FOR FACULTY TO CONDUCT IMPACTFUL RESEARCH AND WORK WITH ARKANSAS STATE EXTENSION TO DISSEMINATE INFORMATION TO PRODUCERS. CAPACITY BUILDING WILL BE DIRECTLY SUPPORTED BY A PROJECT FOCUSED ON IMPROVING CROP RESIDUE BURNING IN THE ARKANSAS DELTA REGION. INTENTIONAL BURNING IS AN IMPORTANT PRACTICE FOR RICE PRODUCERS BECAUSE IT PROVIDES TIMELY, COST-EFFECTIVE REMOVAL OF HARMFUL POST-HARVEST RESIDUE. HOWEVER, BURNING ADVERSELY AFFECTS COMMUNITIES IN SURROUNDING AREAS. WHILE VOLUNTARY BURNING GUIDELINES (VSMG) EXIST, THEY HAVE NOT BEEN VALIDATED ANDCOULD BE IMPROVED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS WITH FARMERS ON IN-FIELD BURN EXPERIMENTS AND THE PROVISION OF BURN RECOMMENDATIONS VIA A WEB APPLICATION. ADDITIONALLY, LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW PRODUCERS MIGHT BE INCENTIVIZED TO COMPLY WITH VSMG OR ADOPT ALTERNATIVE NO-BURN OR LOW-BURN PRACTICES. AS SUCH, THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO USE A SUITE OF COUPLED SMOKE TRANSPORT MODELS AND ON-FARM EXPERIMENTAL BURNS CONDUCTED WITH FARMERS TO IMPROVE VSMG RECOMMENDATIONS. PRODUCER AND COMMUNITY MEMBER SURVEYS WILL BE CONDUCTED TO ELICIT COMMUNITY MEMBERS' WILLINGNES-TO-PAY FOR COMPLIANCE AND PRODUCERS WILLINGNESS-TO-ACCEPT TO COMPLY OR ELIMINATE BURNING. FINALLY, IMPROVED BURN RECOMMENDATIONS WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO A USER-FRIENDLY APPLICATION FOR PRODUCERS AND EXTENSION COLLABORATIONS WILL HELP ENSURE ITS ADOPTION.

THE LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER VALLEY (LMRV) INCLUDES MORE THAN 4 MILLION HA OF IRRIGATED CROPLAND IN PORTIONS OF ARKANSAS, KENTUCKY, LOUISIANA, MISSISSIPPI, MISSOURI, AND TENNESSEE AND IS ONE THE MOST PRODUCTIVE AGRICULTURAL REGIONS IN THE UNITED STATES. NATIONALLY, ARKANSAS AND MISSISSIPPI RANK THIRD AND EIGHTH, RESPECTIVELY, IN TERMS OF IRRIGATED ACRES. WHILE OTHER AREAS DECLINED, THE AMOUNT OF IRRIGATED CROPLAND IN THE LMRV HAS BEEN STEADILY INCREASING AND GREW AT AN AVERAGE ANNUAL RATE OF APPROXIMATELY 2% BETWEEN 2002 AND 2012. AS THE CLIMATE BECOMES DRIER IN THE WESTERN U.S., IRRIGATED CROPLANDS SUCH AS THOSE OF THE LMRV WILL GROW MORE IMPORTANT WITH EACH PASSING DECADE.AS AGRICULTURE SEEKS TO MITIGATE THE IMPACTS OF A CHANGING CLIMATE ON WATER AND SOIL RESOURCES AS WELL AS REDUCE ITS OWN ENVIRONMENTAL FOOTPRINT, FURROW-RICE OFFERS POTENTIAL BENEFITS TO PRODUCERS. HOWEVER, THERE ARE ALSO KNOWN CHALLENGES WITH THE SYSTEM. IN PARTICULAR, GRAIN YIELDS HAVE TENDED TO BE LOWER THAN TRADITIONAL FLOOD SYSTEMS. A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF NITROGEN DYNAMICS AND WEED PRESSURE IN THESE SYSTEMS IS IMPORTANT FOR MANAGMENT OF FURROW IRRIGATED RICE. THE WATER-SAVING POTENTIAL AND OTHER KEY ASPECTS OF THE SYSTEM REMAIN IN QUESTION AND REQUIRE ADDITIONAL RESEARCH TO DETERMINE IF IT HAS BROAD APPLICABILITY TO THE LMRV WHERE THE MAJORITY OF THE NATION'S RICE IS PRODUCED.WINTER COVER CROPS MAY ALSO HELP ADDRESS SOME OF THE CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH THE FURROW-RICE SYSTEM. FOR EXAMPLE, COVER CROPS HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO SUPPRESS WEEDS. PIGWEEDS, IN PARTICULAR, REQUIRE SUNLIGHT TO GERMINATE AND THUS, COVER CROPS MAY HELP SHADE OUT THE PROBLEMATIC PIGWEED AND OTHER WEED SPECIES. MOREOVER, COVER CROP MIXTURES TYPICALLY INCLUDE ONE OR MORE LEGUME SPECIES TO FIX NITROGEN AND THUS, MAY REDUCE N FERTILIZER NEEDED TO COMPENSATE FOR INCREASED NITRIFICATION/DENITRIFICATION LOSSES REPORTED FOR FURROW-IRRIGATION RICE SYSTEMS. REDUCING NITROGEN USE IN AGRICULTURE IS IMPORTANT BECAUSE THE GLOBAL NCYCLE IS HIGHLY PERTURBED. BY ADDRESSING THESE CHALLENGES IN FURROW IRRIGATED RICE PRODUCTION, THE POTENTIAL FOR A SOYBEAN-RICE ROTATION WHERE ANNUAL TILLAGE IS NOT NEEDED TO KNOCK DOWN RICE LEVEES OR BUILD BEDS FOR SOYBEAN PRODUCTION WILL BE ENHANCED PROVIDING GREATER POTENTIAL FOR INPUT REDUCTIONS, GREATER RESILIENCY IN A CLIMATE CHANGING WORLD, AND MAINTAINED/ENHANCED FARM PROFITIABILITY.THIS LARGE-SCALE, INTEGRATED PROJECT AIMS TO FOCUS ON THE AREAS OF RESEARCH AND EDUCATION, WHILE BUILDING THE CAPACITY OF THE COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE AT ARKANSAS STATE UNIVERSITY, SOUTHEAST MISSOURI STATE UNIVERSITY, AND UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE AT MARTIN. THIS COLLABORATIVE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THESE MID-SOUTH INSTITUTIONS' ABILITY TO CONDUCT QUALITY, DYNAMIC RESEARCH AND INNOVATIVE EDUCATION IN THE AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES. BY SOLIDIFYING THIS REGIONAL TEAM, WE ARE BUILDING A LONG-LASTING COLLABORATION TO ADDRESS REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL ISSUES.THIS MULTIDISCIPLINARY, MULTI-INSTITUTIONAL PROJECT WILL TARGET A WIDE RANGING AUDIENCE. FACULTY MEMBERS WILL ENHANCE THEIR RESEARCH AND TEACHING EXPERTISE; HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS WILL RECEIVE CURRICULAR DEVELOPMENT IN AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE; HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WILL BE EXPOSED TO AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE IN THEIR CLASSROOM; REGIONAL FARMERS WILL HAVE ACCESS TO NEW MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES FOR ROW RICE PRODUCTION; UNIVERSITY STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN RESEARCH ACTIVITIES AND HAVE ACCESS TO AN INTENSIVE AGRICULTURAL FIELD COURSE THAT INCLUDES SPECIFIC WRITING AND INSTRUMENTATION WORKSHOPS.THROUGH THIS PROJECT WE WILL COLLECT AND PROVIDE DATA ON NITROGEN USE EFFICIENCY, MOISTURE RETENTION AND IRRIGATION WATER USE, AND WEED SUPPRESSION FROM COVER CROP USE IN ROW RICE PRODUCTION. A CROP BUDGET WILL BE DEVELOPED SPECIFICALLY FOR ROW RICE PRODUCTION WITH COVER CROPS AND PROFITABILITY COMPARED TO CONVENTIONAL MANAGEMENT.DURING THIS THREE YEAR PROJECT, WE WILL HAVE DIRECT IMPACT ON TWO LARGE RICE FARMERS, 10 HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS, 40 COLLEGE STUDENTS, OF WHICH AT LEAST 10 WILL BE FROM REGIONAL MINORITY-SERVING UNIVERSITIES. INDIRECT IMPACT WILL INCLUDE MORE THAN 2000 HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS OVER THE COURSE OF THIS PROJECT AND NUMEROUS FARMERS IN THE REGION.

THE PRIMARY OBJECTIVE OF THIS GRANT IS TO ASSIST HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS OF THE REGION TO MEET THE HIGHER LEARNING COMMISSION'S (HLC) QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENT FOR DUAL CREDIT TEACHERS BY DEVELOPING TWO EIGHTEEN CREDIT HOUR GRADUATE CERTIFICATE PROGRAMS, ONE IN ANIMAL SCIENCE AND ONE IN PLANT SCIENCE THAT WOULD BE OFFERED IN A HYBRID SETTING (ONLINE AND ON-CAMPUS) OVER A PERIOD OF TWO SUMMERS BY THE AGRICULTURE PROGRAM FACULTY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF CENTRAL MISSOURI. BEGINNING SEPTEMBER 1, 2017, THE HLC IMPLEMENTED A NEW REQUIREMENT, HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS MUST HAVE EITHER A MASTER'S DEGREE IN THE FIELD THEY ARE TEACHING A DUAL CREDIT, OR IF THE MASTER'S DEGREE IS NOT IN THE FIELD THEY ARE TEACHING IN THEY NEED TO HAVE 18 GRADUATE CREDIT HOURS IN THE FIELD THEY ARE TEACHING DUAL CREDIT. EXISTING DUAL CREDIT TEACHERS WILL HAVE UNTIL 2022 TO BECOME COMPLIANT WITH THIS NEW REQUIREMENT. THIS GRANT WILL SUBSIDIZE (PAY 75%) OF THE COST FOR TEACHERS WHO ARE ACCEPTED IN THE PROGRAM.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS USDA NLGCA PROJECT IS TO PROVIDE ENHANCED EDUCATIONAL AND OUTREACH OPPORTUNITIES BY WAY OF RESEARCHING MATERNAL RECOGNITION OF PREGNANCY IN MARES. THROUGH THE ACQUISITION OF STATE-OF-THE ART LABORATORY AND CLASSROOM EQUIPMENT, BOTH HIGH SCHOOL AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AND ANIMAL SCIENCE FACULTY WILL BE INVOLVED IN EXPERIMENTAL AND APPLICABLE RESEARCH THAT ADVANCES THE BODY OF KNOWLEDGE IN THE FIELD OF REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY. PROJECT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING COURSE-EMBEDDED RESEARCH PROJECTS, COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH EXPERIENCES AT NORTH DAKOTA STATE UNIVERSITY, AND A SUMMER RESEARCH CAMP FOR UPWARD BOUND STUDENTS LED BY UWRF EQUINE MAJORS. UPWARD BOUND SERVES BOTH HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS FROM LOW-INCOME FAMILIES AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS FROM FAMILIES IN WHICH NEITHER PARENT HOLDS A BACHELOR'S DEGREE. THE GOAL OF UPWARD BOUND IS TO INCREASE THE RATE AT WHICH PARTICIPANTS ENROLL IN AND COMPLETE SECONDARY EDUCATION.THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL USE THE PLACEMENT OF AN INTERUTERINE DEVICE (IUD) TO INDUCE A PSEUDOPREGNANCY IN MARES AND ENABLE THE RESEARCHERS TO STUDY WHETHER THE EPITHELIAL SODIUM CHANNEL (ENAC) RECEPTOR IS INVOLVED WITH THE MATERNAL RECOGNITION OF PREGNANCY PROCESS. RESULTS ARE ANTICIPATED TO ENHANCE THE UNDERSTANDING AND MANAGEMENT OF REPRODUCTIVE PROCESSES AND FERTILITY ALTERNATIVES WITHIN THE SPECIES. IN ADDITION, BECAUSE BLATANT UNWANTED BEHAVIORS IN MARES ARE CLOSELY LINKED TO HORMONAL CHANGES, THE KNOWLEDGE GAINED WILL PROVIDE THE FOUNDATION FOR DESIGNING A SAFER, MORE EFFECTIVE BEHAVIORAL MANAGEMENT OPTION FOR VETERINARIANS, RESEARCHERS, AND MARE OWNERS.

THE CENTER FOR REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE AND RESILIENT SYSTEMS (CRARS)AT CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, CHICO (CHICO STATE), IN COLLABORATION WITH THECALIFORNIA ASSOCIATION OF RESOURCE CONSERVATION DISTRICTS (CARCD), PROPOSES TO CREATE THEAGRICULTURAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS LEARNING COLLABORATIVE (AMS COLLABORATIVE) TO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE AND ENHANCE IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT FOR THE EXPANSION OF SYSTEMS-BASED FARM/RANCH/FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN NORTHERN CALIFORNIA PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. PROJECT ACTIVITIES WILL LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR ONGOING, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT THAT WILL CONTINUE TO ADDRESS IDENTIFIED STAKEHOLDER NEEDS, AS WELL AS OUR LONG-TERM GOALS TO BUILD ADDITIONAL EDUCATIONAL AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT CAPACITY IN SYSTEMS-BASED AGRICULTURAL MANAGEMENT. PROJECT ACTIVITIES ARE RESPONSIVE TO THE RESULTS OF A BROADLY DISSEMINATED NEEDS ASSESSMENT (113 RESPONSES ANALYZED). OUR STAKEHOLDERS INCLUDE PRODUCERS; AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS, INCLUDING COOPERATIVE EXTENSION, CALIFORNIARESOURCE CONSERVATION DISTRICT (RCD), AND NRCS STAFF; AND STUDENTS ENROLLED IN AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES, AND LAND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT.      PROJECT GOALS:1)ESTABLISH FLEXIBLE NON-CREDIT BEARING LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES TO ADDRESS A BROAD RANGE OF STAKEHOLDER NEEDS AND INTERESTS;2)ESTABLISH A COHORT OF PEER MENTORS/ROLE MODELS IN SYSTEMS-BASED AGRICULTURAL MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS; AND3)PROVIDE ADDITIONAL PARTICIPANT-DRIVEN SUPPORT MECHANISMS TO PROMOTE AND ENCOURAGE SUSTAINED KNOWLEDGE BUILDING/SHARING AND CONNECTIONS ACROSS THE COMMUNITY.       PROJECT OBJECTIVES:1)DEVELOP FOUR ONLINE COURSES IN AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS AND SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT THAT WILL SERVE AS A FOUNDATION FOR MULTIPLE EDUCATION AND OUTREACH PATHWAYS;2)IDENTIFY, SUPPORT, AND ASSESS THE EXPERIENCES OF 10 PAIRED TEAMS OF NORTHERN CALIFORNIA PRODUCERS AND RCD TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROVIDERS WHO WILL SERVE AS PEER ROLE MODELS AND MENTORS; AND3)ADD VALUE TO EXISTING CRARS OUTREACH AND ASSISTANCE EFFORTS THROUGH COMMUNITY-DRIVEN WORKSHOPS AND AND AN ONLINE AMS COLLABORATIVE NETWORK.        PROJECT OUTCOMES:1)FOUR ON-LINE COURSES IN SYSTEMS-BASED AGRICULTURE,2)A SUSTAINED PRESENTATION SESSION AT THE CARCD ANNUAL CONFERENCE,3)SUSTAINED VALUE-ADDED ELEMENTS TO CRARS OUTREACH EFFORTS; AND4)DATA-INFORMED (QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE) APPROACHES AND LESSONS LEARNED THAT CAN BE TRANSLATED TO OTHER LOCAL AND REGIONAL CONTEXTS. OVER TIME, WE CAN ADDITIONALLY EXPECT INCREASED LITERACY IN SYSTEMS-BASED AGRICULTURE AT CSU, CHICO.      MEDIUM- AND LONG-TERM OUTCOMESOF THE AMS COLLABORATIVE PROJECT BEYOND THE FUNDING PERIOD INCLUDE:1)ESTABLISH A PROFESSIONAL COURSE SERIES AS A CONTINUING PROGRAM FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS AND PROFESSIONALS,2)CREATE AN INSTITUTIONALLY-APPROVAL 21-CREDIT CERTIFICATE PROGRAM AVAILABLE TO REGIONAL AND NATIONAL AUDIENCES;3)ESTABLISH AN UNDERGRADUATE PROGRAM AND ONLINE MASTER'S PROGRAM IN SYSTEMS-BASED AGRICULTURAL MANAGEMENT; AND4)SUSTAIN THE AMS COLLABORATIVE THROUGH CONTINUING PARTNERSHIPS, COLLABORATIONS AND PROJECTS.

WITH A DECLINE IN LOCAL GROCERS AND RESTAURANTS, PARTS OF RURAL ILLINOIS FACE LIMITED ACCESS TO NUTRITIOUS FOOD, WHICH MAY CONTRIBUTE TO RISING HEALTH CONCERNS, LIKE OBESITY AND DIABETES. MEANWHILE, LOCAL FOOD PRODUCERS FACE DISTRIBUTION CHALLENGES. THE GOAL OF THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT IS TO FACILITATE PLANNING SESSIONS WITH REPRESENTATIVES OF LOCAL FOOD RETAILER, PRODUCER, AND CONSUMER STAKEHOLDER GROUPS TO FORM A FOOD ACCESS NETWORK THAT ADDRESSES THESE CONCERNS THROUGH AN INTEGRATED LARGE-SCALE COMPREHENSIVE INITIATIVE (LCI) GRANT UNDER THE CAPACITY BUILDING GRANTS FOR NON-LAND GRANT COLLEGES OF AGRICULTURE (NLGCA) PROGRAM. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE LCI IS TO IMPROVE LOCAL FOOD SYSTEMS' ABILITY TO SERVE RESIDENTS OF FOOD DESERTS IN RURAL ILLINOIS. FIVE PRIMARY OBJECTIVES CONTRIBUTE TO THE PLANNING PROJECT'S MAIN GOAL OF SECURING A SUBSEQUENT LCI GRANT, INCLUDING: 1) FORM A NETWORK OF STAKEHOLDERS, 2) ASSESS THE EXTENT OF FOOD ACCESS ISSUES AND NUMBER OF LOCAL PRODUCERS IN RURAL ILLINOIS, 3) DEVELOP A RESEARCH AGENDA TO DISCOVER AND OVERCOME IMPEDIMENTS TO FOOD ACCESS, 4) DESIGN A COORDINATED STATEWIDE OUTREACH PROGRAM, AND 5) PREPARE A PROPOSAL FOR A SUBSEQUENT LCI GRANT TO ENACT THE RESEARCH AND OUTREACH PROGRAM. WESTERN ILLINOIS UNIVERSITY FACULTY MEMBERS' STRENGTHS IN MARKETING AND COOPERATIVE BUSINESS COMPLEMENT EXPERTISE OF OTHER GROUPS CURRENTLY WORKING SEPARATELY ON THESE INTERRELATED ISSUES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT ALIGNS DIRECTLY WITH THE LEGISLATIVE REAUTHORIZATION AND THE PRIORITY AREAS OF THE NLGCA PROGRAM, BY SPECIFICALLY ADDRESSING STRATEGIC GOAL #4 (FACILITATE RURAL PROSPERITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT) OF THE 2018-2022 USDA STRATEGIC PLAN, OBJECTIVE 4.1.

SILVERLEAF WHITEFLY (SLW) AND BROWN MARMORATED STINK BUG (BMSB) ARE INVASIVE INSECTS WHICH CAUSE SEVERE LOSSES IN TOMATO. INSECTICIDAL CONTROL OF THESE PESTS ARE HARMFUL TO THE ENVIRONMENT AND APPLICATORS. ACYLSUGARS ARE A PLANT PRODUCED INSECT RESISTANCE COMPOUND FOUND IN TOMATOES. ACYLSUGAR-MEDIATED INSECT RESISTANCE IN TOMATO COULD PROVIDE SAFE ALTERNATIVE CONTROL. DIFFERENT ACYLSUGAR CHEMISTRIES (CHEMOTYPES) DIFFERENTIALLY AFFECT INSECT SPECIES, SO USING SUITABLE LEVELS OF THE MOST EFFECTIVE CHEMOTYPES IS CRITICAL FOR ACYLSUGAR-MEDIATED RESISTANCE OF MULTIPLE PESTS. THE CORNELL UNIVERSITY (CU) TOMATO BREEDING PROGRAM CREATED TOMATO LINES PRODUCING HIGH LEVELS OF ACYLSUGAR WITH DIFFERENT CHEMOTYPES, PROVIDING A PLATFORM FOR TRIALING THE SLW/BMSB CONTROL ACROSS ACYLSUGAR CHEMOTYPES AND TO FACILITATE CREATION OF INSECT RESISTANT TOMATO LINES.OUR OVERALL GOAL FOR THIS INTERACTIVE RESEARCH PROJECT BETWEEN TENNESSEE TECHNOLOGICAL UNIVERSITY (TTU) AND CU IS THE IDENTIFICATION OF TOMATO LINES WITH OPTIMAL ACYLSUGAR-MEDIATED SLW/BMSB CONTROL. OUR RESEARCH WILL BREED ACYLSUGAR PRODUCTION INTO HORTICULTURALLY ACCEPTABLE LINES THAT CAN BE USED BY SEED COMPANIES AND PRODUCERS FOR SUSTAINABLE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY TOMATO PRODUCTION. WE WILL ALSO LOOK AT HOW CHANGES IN THE ACYLSUGAR CHEMISTRIES DIFFERENTIALLY AFFECT FEEDING AND DAMAGE FROM SLW AND BMSB. IN DOING THIS RESEARCH WE WILL HAVE SEVERAL CAPACITY-BUILDING OUTCOMES TO BE ACHIEVED AT TTU INCLUDING 1) CREATING A TTU/CU RESEARCH PARTNERSHIP 2) DEVELOPING A GRADUATE RESEARCH ASSISTANTSHIP FOR AN UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENT AT TTU, 3) PROVIDING SUMMER RESEARCH INTERNSHIPS FOR UNDERREPRESENTED UNDERGRADUATES AT TTU 4) PURCHASE EQUIPMENT AT TTU TO SUPPORT ENTOMOLOGICAL/HORTICULTURAL RESEARCH

CONCENTRATED DAIRY OPERATIONS ARE IMPLICATED IN LAKE AND STREAM EUTROPHICATION AS WELL AS IN THE FORMATION OF OCEAN DEAD ZONES. COST-EFFECTIVE METHODS FOR PRODUCING BIOCHARS THAT CAN ENHANCE BIOREMEDIATION OF PHOSPHOROUS-SATURATED SOILS CAN SIMULTANEOUSLY INCREASE THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY OF DAIRY OPERATIONS. WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT AN INTEGRATED, MULTIDISCIPLINARY PROGRAM FOR THE STUDENT-FOCUSED DEVELOPMENT, TESTING, AND PROMOTION OF PHOSPHORUS-REMEDIATING BIOCHARS. WHILE BIOCHAR IS INCREASINGLY BEING PROMOTED TO ENHANCE CARBON SEQUESTRATION, STIMULATE PLANT GROWTH, AND REMEDIATE SOILS, ITS USE IS CURRENTLY LIMITED DUE TO THE HIGH PRODUCTION COSTS. PRELIMINARY RESEARCH HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT BIOCHARS PRODUCED FROM A BLEND OF MANURE AND WASTE DAIRY HAY HAVE LOWER PRODUCTION COSTS DUE TO REDUCED MOISTURE WHILE DEMONSTRATING ENHANCED PHOSPHORUS REMEDIATION PROPERTIES. OUR MULTI-AGENCY TEAM, CONSISTING OF TEXAS A&M AGRILIFE RESEARCH, AND TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY IS IDEALLY POISED TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE THESE FINDINGS BY COMBINING RESEARCH, TEACHING, AND EXTENSION EXPERTISE FROM ENVIRONMENTAL ENGINEERING, DAIRY MANAGEMENT, AGRONOMY, SOIL SCIENCE, GENOMICS, AND ECONOMICS. COST-EFFECTIVE BIOCHAR PRODUCTION WILL PROVIDE DAIRY FARMERS WITH A VIABLE METHOD FOR OFF-FARM REMOVAL OF EXCESS MANURE NUTRIENTS THROUGH BIOCHAR SALE TO FARMING, GARDENING, AND BIOSWALE OPERATIONS. IT WILL ALSO HELP THEM PROTECT WATER QUALITY BY ENHANCING THE REMOVAL OF LEGACY SOIL PHOSPHORUS. THIS PROJECT'S INTEGRATION OF BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH WITH OUTREACH ACTIVITIES WILL ENHANCE COLLABORATION AMONG INVESTIGATORS WHILE PROVIDING STUDENTS WITH THE COMBINED TECHNICAL AND PRACTICAL SCIENCE EXPERTISE THEY WILL NEED TO ADDRESS "WICKED" PROBLEMS FACING AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES.

COMMODITY PRICES FLUCTUATE CONTINUOUSLY THROUGHOUT THE YEAR DUE TO CHANGES IN THE UNDERLYING SUPPLY AND DEMAND VARIABLES. UNDERSTANDING COMMODITY PRICE BEHAVIOR HELPS FARMERS IN MANAGING THEIR PRODUCTION RISKS AND MAKING PROPER MARKETING DECISIONS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BUILD THE CAPACITY FOR DELIVERING AGRICULTURAL MARKETING COURSES BY ESTABLISHING A STATE OF THE ART MARKETING LAB IN THE HUTSON SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE AT MURRAY STATE UNIVERSITY. THE PLANNED LAB WILL INCORPORATE LATEST COMPUTER HARDWARE, TRADING, AND SIMULATION SOFTWARE, ACCESS TO MARKET INFORMATION, AND DATA RESOURCES MADE AVAILABLE TO STUDENTS TO PROVIDE TRUE "HANDS-ON" EDUCATION IN ORDER TO ENHANCE THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE OF COMMODITY MARKETS IN TODAY'S AGRICULTURE. STUDENTS BETTER UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF VARIOUS STAKEHOLDERS IN THE COMMODITY MARKETS AREA SUCH AS PROCESSORS, HEDGERS, AND SPECULATORS. THROUGH THIS PROJECT, AGRIBUSINESS STUDENTS GAIN VALUABLE SKILLS REGARDING VARIOUS FUNDAMENTAL AND TECHNICAL PRICE FORECASTING METHODS, FAMILIARITY WITH THE BROKERAGE OPERATIONS AND COMMODITY PRICE RISK MANAGEMENT. BESIDES ESTABLISHING A MARKETING LAB, THE PRESENT PROPOSAL ALSO AIMS TO PROVIDE SHORT-TERM RESEARCH PROJECT OPPORTUNITIES TO UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS LEADING TO PRESENTATIONS. ULTIMATELY, THIS PROJECT RESULTS IN READILY EMPLOYABLE AGRIBUSINESS GRADUATES MEETING INDUSTRY NEED IN THE AREA OF COMMODITY MARKETING.

THIS PROJECT IMPROVES THE WELDING EQUIPMENT THROUGH THE PURCHASE OF EIGHT LINCOLN ELECTRIC C300 MULTIPROCESS WELDERS. THE C300 ALLOWS OUR STUDENTS TO LEARN HOW TO COMPLETE THE FOLLOWING WELDING PROCESSES: SHIELDED METAL ARC WELDING (SMAW), GAS METAL ARC WELDING (GMAW), GAS TUNGSTEN ARC WELDING (GTAW) AND FLUX CORE WELDING FROM ONE MACHINE. THE C300 WOULD REPLACE OUTDATED EQUIPMENT AND OFFER FOUR DIFFERENT PROCESSES IN ONE STATION. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT WOULD INCLUDE THE PURCHASE OF TWO TORCHMATE 4400 PLASMA CUTTING TABLES. THE TXST DAS CURRENTLY DOES NOT HAVE AN OPERATIONAL CNC PLASMA CUTTING TABLE IN THE WELDING LABORATORY. THE TORCHMATE 4400 ALLOWS STUDENTS TO LEARN HOW TO USE COMPUTER AIDED DESIGN (CAD) SOFTWARE TO DESIGN ITEMS TO BE CUT USING A CNC PLASMA CUTTING TABLE. THE PURCHASE OF THESE MACHINES WOULD ALSO INCLUDE THE EDUCATIONAL SOFTWARE PACKAGES FOR COMPUTER AIDED DESIGN (CAD) AND COMPUTER AIDED MANUFACTURING (CAM). STUDENTS WILL USE CAD/CAM SOFTWARE, WHICH IS WIDELY UTILIZED IN INDUSTRY TO DESIGN AND DRAW PARTS. THEY WILL GAIN EXPERIENCE IN CREATING PARTS IN A CAD ENVIRONMENT, ENTERING SPECIFICATIONS, SETTING TOLERANCES, AND CHECKING TOOL PATHS. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO UPDATE THE WELDING LABORATORY AT THE TXST DAS FOR THE AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION STUDENTS AND THE NEWLY TRANSITIONED AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS STUDENTS. THE PURPOSE WILL BE FULFILLED BY THE FOLLOWING OBJECTIVES: 1) PROVIDE WELDING TRAINING USING PROCESSES THAT MEET INDUSTRY STANDARDS, 2) PREPARE STUDENTS TO USE PRODUCT DESIGN AND RAPID PRODUCTION FABRICATION, AND 3) PURCHASE EQUIPMENT NEEDED TO CONDUCT VIRTUAL REALITY SEQUENCING RESEARCH.

THEREFORE, THIS PROJECT WILL HAVE A PROFOUND IMPACT UPON UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS. UNDOUBTEDLY, THIS PROJECT IS TIGHTLY ALIGNED TO THE PURPOSE OF NLGCA, I.E. TO MAIN AND EXPAND CAPACITY TO CONDUCT EDUCATION, RESEARCH, AND OUTREACH/EXTENSION ACTIVITIES RELATING TO THE FANH SCIENCES THROUGH THE PURCHASE OF EQUIPMENT. IT ALSO TARGETS AT A USDA STRATEGIC GOAL -IMPROVED INFRASTRUCTURE, BROADBAND ACCESS AND CONNECTIVITY, AND SUPPORT FOR WORKFORCE AVAILABILITY.

WE ALSO SEEK TO SUPPORT THE LOCAL FARMING MOVEMENT BY DEVELOPING A MODERN AND COST-EFFECTIVE SMALL-SCALE HARVESTING MACHINE. THIS PROJECT IS TO INITIATE AN INTEGRATED LEARNING AND RESEARCH-BASED PROGRAM WITH THE GOAL TO PROMOTE BOTH UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS' INTERESTS IN FOOD SAFETY AT FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY (FSU). THE OVERALL RESEARCH GOAL IS TO DEVELOP TWO ASSAYS USING TWO HIGHLY SELECTIVE AGENTS (ANTIBODY AND APTAMER) FOR THE DETECTION OF THE MAJOR FISH ALLERGEN (I.E., PARVALBUMIN). FOUR SUPPORTING RESEARCH OBJECTIVES ARE (1) PARVALBUMIN PURIFICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION; (2) PARVALBUMIN-SPECIFIC DNA APTAMER DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION; DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF (3) AN INDIRECT COMPETITIVE ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY (ICELISA) AND (4) AN APTAMER-ANTIBODY BASED SANDWICH ASSAY FOR THE DETECTION OF FISH PARVALBUMIN IN FOODS. THE OVERALL EDUCATIONAL GOAL IS TO PROVIDE UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WITH MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH EXPERIENCE IN PROTEIN CHEMISTRY, IMMUNOCHEMISTRY, BIOTECHNOLOGY, AND NANOTECHNOLOGY. IT WILL RECRUIT UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, ESPECIALLY FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR PURSUIT IN FOOD SAFETY. THREE SUPPORTING EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES ARE (1) ENHANCE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS' INVOLVEMENT AND INTEREST IN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH AND INTERNSHIP PROGRAMS; (2) IMPROVE THE GRADUATE TRAINING AND EDUCATION IN FOOD SAFETY; AND (3) INITIATE THE PROPOSED PROJECT AS A FAITHFUL LEARNING OPPORTUNITY FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS TO PURSUE THEIR FURTHER STUDY OR FOOD SAFETY RELATED JOBS. THE EXPECTED MAJOR OUTCOMES ARE (1) TWO ASSAYS (ICELISA AND APTAMER-ANTIBODY BASED SANDWICH ASSAY) WILL BE DEVELOPED TO DETECT FISH PARVALBUMIN IN FOODS; (2) THE CAPACITY OF FSU TO PROVIDE EDUCATION AND RESEARCH TRAINING OF UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS IN FOOD SCIENCE WILL BE EXPANDED; AND (3) ONE NATIONAL PRIORITY CONCERN, FOOD SAFETY, WILL BE ADDRESSED.

THIS PROJECT IS TO INITIATE AN INTEGRATED LEARNING AND RESEARCH-BASED PROGRAM WITH THE GOAL TO PROMOTE BOTH UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS' INTERESTS IN FOOD SAFETY AT FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY (FSU). THE OVERALL RESEARCH GOAL IS TO DEVELOP TWO ASSAYS USING TWO HIGHLY SELECTIVE AGENTS (ANTIBODY AND APTAMER) FOR THE DETECTION OF THE MAJOR FISH ALLERGEN (I.E., PARVALBUMIN). FOUR SUPPORTING RESEARCH OBJECTIVES ARE (1) PARVALBUMIN PURIFICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION; (2) PARVALBUMIN-SPECIFIC DNA APTAMER DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION; DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF (3) AN INDIRECT COMPETITIVE ENZYME-LINKED IMMUNOSORBENT ASSAY (ICELISA) AND (4) AN APTAMER-ANTIBODY BASED SANDWICH ASSAY FOR THE DETECTION OF FISH PARVALBUMIN IN FOODS. THE OVERALL EDUCATIONAL GOAL IS TO PROVIDE UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WITH MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH EXPERIENCE IN PROTEIN CHEMISTRY, IMMUNOCHEMISTRY, BIOTECHNOLOGY, AND NANOTECHNOLOGY. IT WILL RECRUIT UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, ESPECIALLY FROM UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR PURSUIT IN FOOD SAFETY. THREE SUPPORTING EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES ARE (1) ENHANCE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS' INVOLVEMENT AND INTEREST IN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH AND INTERNSHIP PROGRAMS; (2) IMPROVE THE GRADUATE TRAINING AND EDUCATION IN FOOD SAFETY; AND (3) INITIATE THE PROPOSED PROJECT AS A FAITHFUL LEARNING OPPORTUNITY FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS TO PURSUE THEIR FURTHER STUDY OR FOOD SAFETY RELATED JOBS. THE EXPECTED MAJOR OUTCOMES ARE (1) TWO ASSAYS (ICELISA AND APTAMER-ANTIBODY BASED SANDWICH ASSAY) WILL BE DEVELOPED TO DETECT FISH PARVALBUMIN IN FOODS; (2) THE CAPACITY OF FSU TO PROVIDE EDUCATION AND RESEARCH TRAINING OF UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS IN FOOD SCIENCE WILL BE EXPANDED; AND (3) ONE NATIONAL PRIORITY CONCERN, FOOD SAFETY, WILL BE ADDRESSED.

THE REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE DEMONSTRATION LAB (RAD-LAB) PROGRAM FOR SOIL SCIENCE UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH EXPERIENCE (RAD-4-SSURE) WILL PROVIDE FIELD AND LABORATORY OPPORTUNITIES, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCES TO A DIVERSE STUDENT POPULATION AT CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY, CHICO THROUGH THE RAD-LAB AND A VARIETY OF APPLIED RESEARCH AND SERVICE LEARNING PROJECTS. THE OBJECTIVE OF RAD-4-SSURE IS TO EXPOSE STUDENTS TO NEW AND EXISTING ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES AND TECHNOLOGIES TO ASSESS AND QUANTIFY SOIL HEALTH AND PROVIDE AN INTEGRATED TRAINING ENVIRONMENT THAT INCLUDES LAB, LEADERSHIP, DATA SCIENCE, AND COMMUNICATION EXPERIENCES. BUILT AROUND A COHORT BASED EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING APPROACH (SOILS OUTSTANDING INTERDISCIPLINARY LEADERS - SOIL), RAD-4-SSURE WILL FOSTER THE DEVELOPMENT OF SKILLED KNOWLEDGEABLE STUDENTS PREPARED TO BECOME LEADERS IN THE RAPIDLY CHANGING AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES WORKFORCE.

THE PRIMARY GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ENHANCE THE CAPACITY AND ABILITY TO PREPARE UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS. THIS WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED THROUGH THE ENHANCEMENT OF THE AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS LABORATORY WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART SAFETY AND PRODUCTION EQUIPMENT. THIS WILL LEAD TO THE DIRECT IMPROVEMENT OF FOUR DIFFERENT AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS COURSES. THIS GRANT WILL SUPPORT THE COORDINATION AND DIRECTION OF THE TAMUK AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS SHOW AND JUDGING AT VARIOUS PROJECT SHOWS AROUND THE STATE. THESE SERVICE LEARNING EVENTS WILL BE DIRECTED BY THE PI AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, ENHANCING STUDENTS' DEVELOPMENT OF COLLABORATIVE LEADERSHIP AND APPLIED AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS SKILLS. TO ENHANCE THEIR LEADERSHIP SKILLS STUDENTS WILL TAKE PART IN LPI STUDENT AND 360&ORDM; LEADERSHIP ASSESSMENTS THROUGHOUT THE LIFE OF THE PROJECT, TO EVALUATE HOLISTICALLY THEIR LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT. THE AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS FACULTY, WORKING WITH LINCOLN ELECTRIC©, AIRGAS & BRIGGS & STRATTON, WILL ATTEND INDUSTRY PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT WORKSHOPS EACH YEAR. THE DIRECT BENEFIT OF THIS FACULTY TRAINING WILL BE SHARED WITH UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN THE FOUR AGRICULTURAL MECHANIC COURSES, AND WITH SECONDARY TEACHERS AT PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT EVENTS OFFERED AT TAMUK EACH YEAR. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO POSITIVELY IMPACT THE ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENT AND CAREER READINESS OF UNDERREPRESENTED STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURE. ?

negativeFlows.title: RESEARCH CHALLENGE - VEGETATIVE PROPAGATION IS REQUIRED TO MAINTAIN THE IDENTITY AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF INDIVIDUAL PLANTS WITHIN A SPECIFIC GRAPE CULTIVAR OR CLONE. THE ROOTING ABILITY OF THE CULTIVAR OR CLONE IS KEY TO THE SUCCESS OF THIS PROCEDURE. THE UNIQUE CHARACTERISTICS OF VITIS AESTIVALIS-DERIVED 'NORTON' IN DISEASE RESISTANCE AND COLD HARDINESS HAVE HEIGHTENED ITS ATTRACTIVENESS TO GRAPE GROWERS DUE TO INCREASING CONCERNS REGARDING ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AND PESTICIDE AVOIDANCE. HOWEVER, PROPAGATION OF NORTON THROUGH HARDWOOD CUTTINGS HAS BEEN A MAJOR OBSTACLE IN PROVIDING ENOUGH PLANTS TO MEET COMMERCIAL DEMAND. THUS, PLANTING STOCK IS LIMITED AND COSTLY. IN ADDITION, RESEARCH IN THE GENETICS OF 'NORTON' ROOTING ABILITY HAS NOT YET BEEN EXPLORED OR UNDERSTOOD. CLASSICAL BREEDING FOR ENHANCED ROOTING ABILITY FROM HARDWOOD CUTTINGS HAS BEEN A CRUCIAL COMPONENT FOR COMMERCIAL DEPLOYMENT OF INTENSIVELY CULTURED VINEYARDS; HOWEVER, SUCH EFFORTS OFTEN TAKE MORE THAN 20 YEARS TO FULLY EVALUATE AND RELEASE NEW CULTIVARS. BECAUSE OF THE LONG BREEDING CYCLE IN WOODY PLANT SPECIES LIKE GRAPE, DEVELOPING DNA MARKERS LINKED TO GENES OR QUANTITATIVE TRAIT LOCI (QTLS) FOR HORTICULTURAL TRAITS CAN GREATLY ACCELERATE THE BREEDING PROCESS AND ALLOW A MUCH MORE ACCURATE SELECTION OF PROGENY. THE MOST BASIC CHALLENGE OF THIS PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO SEEK 1) KNOWLEDGE OF ANY FACTOR THAT CONSTRAINS OR PROMOTES ROOTING ABILITY; AND 2) GUIDELINES THAT ALLOW THE INCORPORATION OF ROOTING ABILITY AS A SELECTION CRITERION IN STRATEGIC OR OPERATIONAL BREEDING PLANS.EXTENSION/EDUCATION CHALLENGE - CURRENT FORMAL ADVANCED EDUCATIONAL TRAINING IN AGRICULTURE IS MAINLY DRIVEN BY RESEARCH WHICH IS FACILITATED BY PAID RESEARCH ASSISTANTSHIPS. THIS CURRENT AND HISTORICAL PROCESS ENRICHES A STUDENT IN RESEARCH-BASED ACTIVITIES AND FORMAL CLASSROOM COURSEWORK. FEW STUDENTS UPON COMPLETING A DEGREE HAVE PARTICIPATED OR EXPERIENCED EXTENSION. FOR THOSE STUDENTS WHO HAVE ENCOUNTERED EXTENSION OFTEN BELIEVE EXTENSION ACTIVITIES INCLUDE ONLY FORMAL ORAL PRESENTATIONS OR LOGISTICAL PLANNING OF EXTENSION WORKSHOPS. UNIVERSITY EXTENSION SPECIALISTS PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN ESTABLISHING LINKAGES BETWEEN RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS. WHEREAS THE RESEARCH PROPOSED GENERATES USEFUL TECHNOLOGY, EXTENSION FOCUSES ON PROVIDING THE ACCEPTANCE AND ADOPTION OF THE TECHNOLOGY FOR WHICH IT WAS INTENDED. IN MOST SITUATIONS, TECHNOLOGY GENERATED THROUGH RESEARCH IS FOCUSED ON THE USER OR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCER. THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCER AND EXTENSION SPECIALIST ENCOMPASSES BI-DIRECTIONAL LEARNING WHEREAS THE EXTENSION SPECIALIST ALSO LEARNS FROM THE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS DURING THE TEACHING. EXPOSING GRADUATE STUDENTS TO EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OF WORKING WITH AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS ONE ON ONE, IN SMALL GROUPS, WORKSHOPS OR CONFERENCES WILL BROADEN THE DEPTH OF GRADUATE STUDENTS FOR THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR. ALSO, THE COALITION FOR A SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE (CSAW) RECENTLY PUBLISHED AN IN-DEPTH ASSESSMENT ENTITLED "2013 AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE WORKFORCE CENSUS". THIS DOCUMENT EMPHASIZED THAT THE GROWTH OF AGRICULTURE RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND EXTENSION RESOURCES HAS NOT BEEN ABLE TO KEEP PACE WITH INDUSTRY EXPANSION. IT IS URGENT TO ENCOURAGE MORE STUDENTS TO PURSUE ADVANCED DEGREES IN AGRICULTURE. THE COLLABORATION AMONG THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AT MISSOURI STATE UNIVERSITY (MSU), GRAPE AND WINE INSTITUTE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI (MU) AND VITISGEN2 AT THE CORNELL UNIVERSITY WILL ASSIST IN TRAINING MSU STUDENTS IN THE MULTIPLE RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND EXTENSION DISCIPLINES REQUIRED FOR MODERN PLANT BREEDING.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE OVERALL GOAL OF SAFE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH AND ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF RURAL COMMUNITIES BY DEVELOPING A SUSTAINABLE FOOD SYSTEM MODEL. THE OBJECTIVES ARE: 1) UTILIZE SOIL MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO IMPROVE CROP AND PASTURE PRODUCTION FOR ENHANCED PRODUCTIVITY AND FOOD QUALITY ACROSS DIFFERENT FOOD SYSTEMS; AND 2) ESTABLISH A FOOD SYSTEM TRAINING CENTER TO PROVIDE SUPPORT IN THE AREAS PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, PRESERVATION, SAFETY, AND FOOD SCIENCE EDUCATION. RESEARCHERS WILL UTILIZE A DAIRY FOOD SYSTEM AND VEGETABLE FOOD SYSTEM TO INVESTIGATE THE IMPACT OF SOIL MANAGEMENT PRACTICES ON CROP, ANIMAL AND FOOD PRODUCTION AND ECONOMICS AND EDUCATION. RESEARCH WILL INFORM THE ENHANCEMENT OF CURRENT AND CREATION OF NEW UNDERGRADUATE COURSES IN PLANT AND SOIL SCIENCE, ANIMAL SCIENCE, FOOD SCIENCE, AGRICULTURE ECONOMICS, AND AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION. OUTREACH INITIATIVES WILL TARGET FARMERS, HIGH SCHOOL AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION TEACHERS, UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS THROUGH FIELD DAY ACTIVITIES, SEMINARS, WEBSITE CREATION, MOBILE FOOD SCIENCE LABORATORY KITS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WITH 2018-2022 USDA STRATEGIC PLAN, GOAL 4, PROMOTING RURAL PROSPERITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND THE NLGCA PROGRAM PRIORITY TO INCREASE THE NUMBER AND DIVERSITY OF STUDENTS ENTERING FOOD AND AGRICULTURE-RELATED SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (STEM) DISCIPLINES. THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT (DISCIPLINE CODES D AND G) ADDRESSES RESEARCH NEED AREAS OF STUDIES AND EXPERIMENTATION IN FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES, EDUCATION NEED AREAS OF SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTATION FOR EDUCATION, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, AND COLLABORATIVE INTERACTIONS WITH OTHER ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS, AND OUTREACH/EXTENSION NEED AREAS OF 4-H, OR OTHER, SIMILAR YOUTH DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITY, FANH SCIENCES, AND NATURAL RESOURCES.

LOW SOCIOECONOMIC STUDENTS AND UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS OFTEN HAVE LITTLE EXPOSURE TO HIGHER EDUCATION AND ARE FREQUENTLY UNAWARE OF CAREER OPPORTUNITIES IN THE FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES. THIS LACK OF FAMILIARITY EXTENDS INTO STUDENT FINANCIAL AID OPPORTUNITIES, MENTORING PROGRAMS, AND TEAM-BUILDING AND PERSONAL DEVELOPMENT SKILLS THAT ENABLE INDIVIDUALS TO ACHIEVE AT A HIGH LEVEL. AGRICULTURE FACULTY AT SAM HOUSTON STATE UNIVERSITRY AND STEPHEN F. AUSTIN STATE UNIVERSITY WILL COLLABORATE ON THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT TO IMMERSE THE TARGET POPULATION INTO VARIOUS DISCIPLINES OF AGRICULTURE AND THEIR RESPECTIVE CAREER OPPORTUNITIES THROUGH INTERACTIVE EDUCATIONAL SESSIONS. THE RELEVANT NEED AREAS WITHIN THE EDUCATION AREA INCLUDE: STUDENT RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND EDUCATIONAL EQUITY; EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING; PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR FACULTY MEMBERS; AND, COLLABORATIVE INTERACTION WITH OTHER ACADEMIC INSTITUTIONS. REGARDING THE OUTREACH/EXTENSION AREA, THE FOLLOWING NEED AREAS WILL BE ADDRESSED: FANH SCIENCES; LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT; AND, COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. SPECIFIC ACADEMIC EMPHAIS WILLINCLUDE WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT/ANIMAL SCIENCE, AGRICULTURALENGINEERING TECHNOLOGY,AGRIBUSINESS,POULTRY SCIENCE, AND HORTICULTURE. THE OVERALL GOALS OF THE PROJECT ARE TO: (1) INCREASE THE RATE AT WHICH LOW SOCIO-ECONOMIC STDUENTS AND UNDER-REPRESENTED POPULATIONS PURSUE A HIGHER EDUCATION AND CAREER IN AGRICULTURE; (2) UTILIZE INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIPS TO BETTER INFORM THE TARGET POPULATION OF OPPORTUNITIES IN COMPANIES, AND HELP PARTNERS UNDERSTAND BARRIERS FACED BY THE TARGET POPULATION IN OBTAINING A COLLEGE DEGREE; AND, (3) FOSTER A GREATER UNDERSTANDING BY FACULTY AT PARTCIPATING INSTITUTIONS OF CURRENT RESEARCH BEING CONDUCETED AT BOTH INSTITUTIONS AND EXPLORE OPPORTUNITIES FOR RESEARCH COLLABORATION.

URBAN LAND AREAS HAVE BEEN EXPANDING GLOBALLY AT A VERY RAPID RATE, EVEN FASTER THAN POPULATION GROWTH. AS THEY EXPAND INTO PREVIOUSLY AGRICULTURAL AREAS, THEY HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO CONSTRAIN FOOD SUPPLY SYSTEMS AND DIMINISH FOOD SECURITY. THIS PUTS INCREASING PRESSURE ON REMAINING AGRICULTURAL LANDS TO PRODUCE THE SAME OR MORE BIOMASS ON LESS LAND FOR A LARGER POPULATION, YET THERE IS LITTLE SCIENTIFIC EVALUATION OF HOW THE GROWTH OF URBAN CENTERS WILL AFFECT REGIONAL AGRICULTURE. LEFT UNADDRESSED, THIS INHERENT TRADE-OFF BETWEEN URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL LAND RESOURCES COULD LEAD TO A DECREASED RESILIENCE IN AND AROUND URBAN AREAS, ESPECIALLY THOSE ALREADY VULNERABLE TO ENVIRONMENTAL RISKS.IN RAPIDLY URBANIZING AREAS SUCH AS PHOENIX AND OTHER SOUTHWESTERN CITIES, THE TRADE-OFFS BETWEEN URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL RESOURCE NEEDS ARE EXACERBATED BY LIMITED RESOURCE AVAILABILITY, ESPECIALLY FOR WATER. THEREFORE, MORE RESEARCH IS NEEDED TO CREATE SYNERGIES BETWEEN URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL RESOURCE DEMANDS, RATHER THAN COMPETITION. SOME PROMISING AREAS OF OPPORTUNITY AT THIS COMPETING RESOURCE-DEMAND NEXUS INCLUDE THE USE OF EXCESS STORMWATER AND TREATED MUNICIPAL WASTEWATER FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, USE OF BIOSOLIDS FROM URBAN WASTEWATER TREATMENT, COMPOST FROM URBAN FOOD WASTE AS AGRICULTURAL FERTILIZER, AND MANURE FROM AGRICULTURAL OPERATIONS FOR URBAN AGRICULTURE NUTRIENT, WATER, AND SOIL HEALTH NEEDS.GIVEN THAT AGRICULTURE IS A VITAL PART OF THE SOUTHWEST'S ECONOMY, AND ENCROACHMENT OF AGRICULTURE BY URBAN EXPANSION, IN ADDITION TO CONCERNS OF DECREASING WATER SUPPLY, HAS THE POTENTIAL TO SEVERELY IMPACT LIVELIHOODS AND FOOD SECURITY IN THE REGION,THEOVERALL GOAL OF THIS GRANT WILL BE TO IMPROVE ARIZONA STATE UNIVERSITY'S (ASUS) CAPACITY TO PERFORM AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EDUCATION TO ADDRESS CHALLENGES AND IDENTIFY EMERGING OPPORTUNITIES AT THE URBAN-AGRICULTURE NEXUS IN THE DESERT SOUTHWEST.THE GOALS AND ACTIVITIES OF THIS PROJECT DIRECTLY ADDRESS GOAL 6 OF THE USDA'S RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND ECONOMICS ACTION PLAN BY HELPING TORECRUIT, CULTIVATE, AND DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS, ENGINEERS, AND LEADERSIN AGRICULTURE THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NEW UNDERGRADUATE COURSE AND THE MULTIPLE OPPORTUNITIES PROVIDED TO STUDENTS TO GAIN LEADERSHIP AND MENTORING EXPERIENCE. THIS PROJECT IS ALSO IN LINE WITH USDA'S STRATEGIC PLAN, GOAL 1, THAT AIMS TOASSIST RURAL COMMUNITIES TO CREATE PROSPERITY, THROUGH OUTREACH AND EDUCATION EFFORTS. THIS PROJECT SUPPORTS MULTIPLE SUBGOALS OF GOAL 1 OF THE NIFA STRATEGIC PLAN AS OUR GOAL TO CONNECT URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL STAKEHOLDERS WILL ULTIMATELY HELPADVANCE FOOD SECURITYIN THE REGION (SUBGOAL 1.1.) AND OUR EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES WILLSUPPORT A DIVERSE WORKFORCE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE(SUBGOAL 1.6). FURTHERMORE, OUR RESEARCH OBJECTIVES DIRECTLY SUPPORT SUBGOAL 1.3 THROUGH THE IMPROVEDEVALUATION OF RECLAIMED RESOURCES IN ARID ENVIRONMENT AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION.WE WILL ACHIEVE OUR PROJECTGOALS AND OBJECTIVES BY EXPANDING ASU'S CAPABILITY TO PERFORM AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EDUCATION, AND BY ENGAGING LOCAL URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES AROUND THE TOPIC OF ADDRESSING CHALLENGES AND IDENTIFYING EMERGING OPPORTUNITIES AT THE URBAN-AGRICULTURE NEXUS IN THE DESERT SOUTHWEST. TO ENHANCE ASU'S AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION CAPACITY, WE WILL DEVELOP AN UNDERGRADUATE-LEVEL EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING COURSE JOINTLY WITH MESA COMMUNITY COLLEGE. THIS COURSE WILL CONSIST OF HANDS-ON RESEARCH PROJECTS RELATED TO URBAN-AGRICULTURE NEXUS, INCLUDING FIELD, LAB, AND DATA ANALYSIS TRAINING FOR THE STUDENTS. TO INCREASE ASU'S ABILITY TO PERFORM AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH, WE ARE PARTNERING WITH THE USDA ARID LANDS AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH CENTER TO MENTOR TWO MASTERS LEVEL PROJECTS FOCUSED ON UNDERSTANDING RISKS AND BENEFITS OF USING URBAN RESOURCES (BIOSOLIDS, WASTEWATER, COMPOSTS, ETC.) IN ARID LAND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION. TO ENGAGE THE URBAN AND AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES, WE WILL HOST KICK-OFF AND SUMMATIVE WORKSHOPS, CREATE A STUDENT-LED WEBINAR SERIES, AND CREATE A STAKEHOLDER ADVISORY GROUP TO INFORM AND ASSESS PROJECT ACTIVITIES. IF THE GOALS OF THE PROJECT ARE MET, WE HOPE TO CREATE A LONG-TERM CULTURE OF AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH INTEREST AT ASU AS WELL AS TO FOSTER NEW CONNECTIONS AND COLLABORATIONS TO CREATE SYNERGISTIC OPPORTUNITIES AT THE URBAN-AGRICULTURE NEXUS.

THE GLOBAL AGLEADER: DEVELOPMENT OF LEADERSHIP AND GLOBAL COMPETENCY TO ENHANCE RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION OF MINORITY STUDENTS PROJECT ADDRESSES THE OBSTACLES REGULARLY FACED IN RECRUITING AND RETAINING THE STUDENTS FROM MINORITY COMMUNITIES IN UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE AGRICULTURAL PROGRAMS. THOUGH THERE ARE PREDICTIONS OF IMPRESSIVE JOB GROWTH IN AGRICULTURE, THERE IS A DOCUMENTED LACK OF SUPPLY OF TRAINED WORKFORCE THAT CAN CATER TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF A RAPIDLY TRANSFORMING AGRICULTURE SECTOR. BUT YOUNG STUDENTS FROM MINORITY COMMUNITIES ARE UNAWARE OF SUCH JOB OPPORTUNITIES, HAVE PERCEIVED ENTRY BARRIERS, AND LACK PROFESSIONAL NETWORKS. WITH MINORITY STUDENTS IN MIND, THE PROJECT WILL DEVELOP A FORWARD-LOOKING AND MULTI-PRONGED APPROACH BY TAKING ADVANTAGE OF THE FONDNESS FOR SOCIAL MEDIA AND TECHNOLOGY AMONG YOUNGER GENERATIONS. IT WILL USE WEB-BASED CONTENTS TO HELP THE STUDENTS IN FORMING PROFESSIONAL SOCIAL NETWORKS AND IN INCREASING THEIR AWARENESS ABOUT THE CAREER OPPORTUNITIES IN AGRICULTURE. THE PROJECT PROPOSES INTERNATIONAL AND DOMESTIC EXPERIENCES AT REPUTABLE ORGANIZATIONS, MENTORING, INTERNSHIPS, AND SUMMER INSTITUTES TO HELP STUDENTS IN CAREER DECISIONS. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE THE ABILITY OF THE TEXAS STATE UNIVERSITY'S (TEXAS STATE) TO I) PROVIDE BETTER EDUCATION TO AGRICULTURAL STUDENTS WITH EMPHASIS ON MINORITY STUDENTS, AND II) CATER TO THE NEEDS OF OTHER STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS FARMERS AND AGRIBUSINESSES. IT WILL ALSO FOSTER TEXAS STATE'S LINKS WITH REPUTABLE INTERNATIONAL AGRICULTURAL INSTITUTIONS. INTENDED RESULTS FROM THE PROJECT INCLUDE: BETTER RECRUITMENT/RETENTION OF MINORITY STUDENTS; AND PREPARING A DYNAMIC BASE OF STUDENTS WITH BOTH TECHNICAL SKILLS AND SOFT-SKILLS REQUIRED TO LEAD IN THEIR CHOSEN CAREER.

THE MAJORITY (55%) OF THE WORLD'S POPULATION LIVES IN URBAN ENVIRONMENTS TODAY, AND BY 2050 THE WORLD'S URBAN POPULATION IS EXPECTED TO BE THE SAME SIZE AS THE WORLD'S TOTAL POPULATION IN 2002. FOOD PRODUCTION IS NO LONGER THE KEY ISSUE TO FEEDING THE WORLD; FARMERS PRODUCE ENOUGH FOOD TO FEED 1.5X THE WORLD'S POPULATION. HOWEVER, THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURE ORGANIZATION OF THE UNITED NATIONS (FAO) ESTIMATES THAT 14% OF ALL FOOD PRODUCED WORLDWIDE IS LOST BETWEEN THE FARM AND CONSUMERS.FOOD PRESERVATION IS OBVIOUSLY THE KEY, AND FOOD FERMENTATION IS A TIME-TESTED AND ESSENTIAL FOOD PRESERVATION TOOL.UNFORTUNATELY, IN MOST DEVELOPED COUNTRIES (INCLUDING THE US), AWARENESS OF EVEN THE MOST BASIC APPLICATIONS OF FERMENTATION IS ALMOST NONEXISTENT AND HOME FERMENTATION IS CONSIDERED AN ANTIQUATED PRACTICE. AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION MUST NOW, THEREFORE, FOCUS ON WAYS OF INTRODUCING STUDENTS TO THIS NEW SCIENCE AND ATTRACT THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS WHO WILL ADDRESS OUR COMMON NEED TO FEED OURSELVES.FERMENTATION SCIENCE, AN APPLIED, STEM-BASED DEGREE, IS FOCUSED ON THE SCIENCE OF FERMENTATION. FERMENTATION IS USED TO PRODUCE A BROAD RANGE OF FAMILIAR VALUE-ADDED AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS INCLUDING BREAD, CHEESE, YOGURT, PICKLES, AND PEPPERONI, BUT IT IS NOT WELL KNOWN THAT IT IS ALSO USED TO PRODUCE PROBIOTICS, CERTAIN PHARMACEUTICALS AND INDUSTRIAL CHEMICALS, AND TO TREAT WASTEWATER. IN SHORT, HUMANITY DEPENDS ON FERMENTATION FOR SURVIVAL BUT IS NOT AWARE OF THE FACT. THIS RESEARCH SEEKS TO TRAIN STEM TEACHERS, PARTICULARLY AT TENNESSEE'S REGIONAL COMMUNITY COLLEGES, TO INCORPORATE FERMENTATION SCIENCE-RELATED TOPICS INTO THEIR EXISTING CLASSES, THEREBY EXPOSING STUDENTS TO THE NEW FERMENTATION SCIENCE DEGREE PROGRAM AT MIDDLE TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY, AND THE POTENTIAL JOBS AVAILABLE UPON COMPLETION OF IT.THIS PROPOSAL FURTHER SEEKS TO UTILIZE PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING (PBL) AS THE PRIMARY TOOL FOR INTEGRATING FERMENTATION SCIENCE INTO EXISTING STEM CURRICULA. THE PEDAGOGY OF PBL HAS BEEN EXTENSIVELY RESEARCHED AND THE EVIDENCE IS NOW CLEAR THAT THE USE OF PBL INCREASES STUDENT COMPREHENSION OF COURSE CONTENT THROUGH THE USE OF REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS OR SCENARIOS. BY ANCHORING STEM CONCEPTS TO REAL-WORLD APPLICATIONS, STUDENTS GAIN AN APPRECIATION OF BOTH THE SCIENTIFIC CONCEPTS AND THE APPLICATION OF THOSE CONCEPTS TO SOLVING REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS.

POLLINATORS HAVE SEEN MAJOR DECLINES IN RECENT DECADES. PESTICIDE EXPOSURE, PESTS, DISEASES, AND A SIGNIFICANT LOSS OF HABITAT DUE TO URBANIZATION HAVE PLAYED AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE LOSS OF POLLINATORS. LOSS OF HABITAT HAS BEEN EXACERBATED BY INCREASED DROUGHT BROUGHT ABOUT BY CLIMATE CHANGE. THE PLANT DRIPS (PLANT DROUGHT RESPONSE AND INSECT POLLINATOR STUDIES) PROJECT AT TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY-COMMERCE AND TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY SEEKS TO LEARN HOW POLLINATOR-FRIENDLY PERENNIALS IN ORNAMENTAL LANDSCAPES PROVIDE A SOLUTION. THIS RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROJECT LEVERAGES CURRENT A&M-COMMERCE AND TARLETON RESOURCES TO CREATE A RESEARCH AND EDUCATION GARDENS THAT ADDRESS QUESTIONS ABOUT THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN MOISTURE STRESS, ORNAMENTAL PLANTS AND POLLINATORS, AND THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE THREE UNDER DISCIPLINE CODES P (PLANT SCIENCES AND HORTICULTURE), D (SOIL SCIENCES), AND T (ENTOMOLOGY - PLANT). WE WANT TO FIND PLANTS THAT WILL SURVIVE ON DRIPS OF WATER WHILE PROVIDING DRIPS OF NECTAR AND POLLEN FOR FORAGING POLLINATORS, ENHANCING BOTH THE AESTHETIC AND ECOLOGICAL ROLES OF OUR LANDSCAPES. THE PROJECT HAS THREE OBJECTIVES:1. EVALUATE LANDSCAPE PERENNIALS ACROSS MULTIPLE SOIL MOISTURE LEVELS,2. EVALUATE POLLINATOR BEHAVIORS RELATED TO FLORAL TIMING AND FLOWER QUALITY AND HOW THESE CHANGE DURING PERIODS OF WATER DEFICITS, AND3. CREATE DEMONSTRATION LANDSCAPES THAT IMPROVE INSTRUCTION AND EXPLORATION IN PLANT SCIENCE, SOIL SCIENCE, HORTICULTURE, ENTOMOLOGY, AND SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE EDUCATION AT A&M-COMMERCE AND TARLETON.THESE OBJECTIVES ARE BUILD EDUCATION AND RESEARCH CAPACITY AT A&M-COMMERCE AND TARLETON, MAINTAINING AND EXPANDING THE INSTITUTIONS' CAPACITY TO CONDUCT EDUCATIONAL AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES.

CONSERVATION PRACTICES HAVE SHOWN GREAT RESULTS IN TERMS OF SOIL-FERTILITY INCREASE, SOIL-MOISTURE RETENTION, LONG-TERM-YIELD INCREASE, AND FOOD-SECURITY IMPROVEMENT. UNFORTUNATELY, THESE GAINS COULD BE THREATENED IN THE TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY BY A CHANGING CLIMATE. MIDDLE TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY (MTSU) AND THE UNIVERSITY OF MISSISSIPPI (UM) ARE COLLABORATING ON THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT TO QUANTIFY WATERSHED RESPONSES TO CONSERVATION PRACTICES UNDER A CHANGING CLIMATE AND ASSESS THE RELATIVE EFFECTIVENESS OF THESE CONSERVATION PRACTICES IN DIFFERENT ENVIRONMENTS. IN ADDITION, WE AIM TO HELP TRAIN THE NEXT GENERATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTISTS AND ENGINEERS TO BE MORE AWARE OF THE AGRICULTURAL CHALLENGES OF THE TWENTY-FIRST CENTURY. OUR MAIN PROJECT OBJECTIVES ARE (1) TO DEVELOP WATERSHED MODELS EXPRESSING THE CURRENT CONDITIONS OF TEN TO FIFTEEN WATERSHEDS AROUND THE COUNTRY REPRESENTING A VARIETY OF CLIMATIC, SOIL, AND AGRICULTURAL REGIMES, (2) TO QUANTIFY THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CONSERVATION PRACTICES UNDER VARIOUS PHYSICAL AND CLIMATIC CONDITIONS, (3) TO QUANTIFY THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON CONSERVATION PRACTICES IN THE STUDIED WATERSHEDS, (4) TO DEVELOP EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING PROJECTS FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, AND (5) TO DEVELOP CURRICULUMS IN OUR PARTNERING INSTITUTIONS FOCUSED ON ENVIRONMENTAL AGRICULTURE. HENCE THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT IS AIMED AT INCREASING THE ADAPTABILITY POTENTIAL OF U.S. AGRICULTURE TO FUTURE CLIMATE ESTIMATES, AND PREPARING THE ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING WORKFORCE WITH SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE TO FACE THESE CHALLENGES. THE PROJECT INVOLVES THE FOLLOWING ACADEMIC CODES: C (CONSERVATION), D (SOIL), L (ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES), AND W (WATER). THE PROJECT ADDRESSES THE FOLLOWING NEED AREAS: APPLIED STUDIES, CURRICULUM DESIGN, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND COLLABORATIVE INTERACTION.

IN RESPONSE TO THE INCREASING AVERAGE U.S. FARMER AGE AND THE IDENTIFIED BARRIERS BEGINNING FARMERS FACE, FEDERAL AND STATE GOVERNMENTS HAVE CREATED OR MAINTAINED PROGRAMS TO SUPPORT BEGINNING FARMERS. THESE PROGRAMS ATTEMPT TO ADDRESS IDENTIFIED CHALLENGES BEGINNING FARMERS FACE TO EASE THEIR BURDEN. FROM AS FAR BACK AS THE 1930S, PROGRAMS HAVE BEEN IN PLACE TO ASSIST FARMERS FROM HELPING THEM TO SECURE LOW INTEREST LOANS, LEASE LAND, RECEIVE TRAININGS OR SECURE CROP INSURANCE. HOWEVER, EVEN WITH THESE PROGRAMS IN PLACE, OUR CONCERNS FOR THE FUTURE OF PRODUCTION AGRICULTURE HAVE NOT CHANGED. THIS RESEARCH BREAKS DOWN THE MECHANISMS OF THESE GOVERNMENT PROGRAMS AND IDENTIFIES FINANCIAL AND/OR SOCIAL BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATION EVALUATES THE ABILITY OF PROGRAMS TO MEET THE NEEDS OF BEGINNING FARMERS, AND IDENTIFIES THE MOST EFFECTIVE WAYS TO DISSEMINATE THE PROGRAM INFORMATION TO INTERESTED PARTIES. THROUGH THE USE OF FOCUS GROUPS AND SURVEYS WE WILL BE ABLE TO ADDRESS MANY OF THE PURPOSES OF THE NLGCA PROGRAM. THROUGH CAREFUL EVALUATION OF THE DATA WE WILL BE ABLE TO ADDRESS THE NUMBER OF AND DIVERSITY OF INDIVIDUALS GETTING INTO PRODUCTION AGRICULTURE. WE WILL DEVELOP LINKAGES WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI AND OTHER AGRICULTURAL STAKEHOLDERS TO DEVELOP A DIALOGUE ON AN INCREDIBLY IMPORTANT TOPIC, WHILE TRAINING TWO MASTERS' LEVEL STUDENTS. WE WILL ALSO BE ABLE TO DISSEMINATE THESE CONCERNS AND ISSUES THROUGHOUT THE PROCESS AND TOWARDS THE DEVELOPMENT OF WORKABLE SOLUTIONS.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** GIVEN THE IMPORTANCE OF SUSTAINABLE FORAGE CROP PRODUCTION, INCREASING SOIL HEALTH, AND GROWING DEMAND FOR QUALIFIED NEW PROFESSIONALS PREPARED IN THESE AREAS, THE DEVELOPMENT OF PROFESSIONALS IN FORAGES, GRAZING MANAGEMENT, AND SOIL HEALTH ASSESSMENTS HAVE BECOME MORE ESSENTIAL THAN EVER.IMPROVING CROP ALTERNATIVE OPTIONS IS CRITICAL FOR A STRONG AGRICULTURAL ECONOMY (MARQUES ET AL., 2020). WITH INCREASING EXTREME CLIMATE EVENTS LEADING TO DROUGHT AND FORAGE CROP WINTER-KILL, WELL-INFORMED ADJUSTMENTS TO CROP PRODUCTION MANAGEMENT ARE NEEDED.THIS PROPOSAL IS A SYNERGY BETWEEN STUDENT TRAINING, EXTENSION EFFORTS, AND EDUCATION AND OUTREACH TO WATERSHED PRODUCERS INTERESTED IN APPLIED FIELD RESEARCH ON ALTERNATIVE FORAGE CROPS AND SUMMER ANNUAL FORAGES USING FIELD INSTRUMENTATION FOR MONITORING FORAGES (CANOPY ANALYZER) AND SOIL HEALTH (HANDHELD TIME DOMAIN REFLECTOMETERS). THESE PORTABLE INSTRUMENTS WILL ALSO ALLOW INSTRUCTORS TO CONDUCT FIELD-LABORATORY EXERCISES, AND EXTENSION TRAINING IN THE AREA OF PLANT-SOIL INTERFACE WITH APPLICATIONS IN FORAGE AND CROP PRODUCTION, GRAZING MANAGEMENT, AND SOIL HEALTH. RESULTS ON FORAGE AND SOIL TESTING WILL ALSO BE MADE AVAILABLE TO FARMERS TO DEMONSTRATE SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION METHODS THAT HAVE MINIMUM IMPACT ON THE ENVIRONMENT.

THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED LARGE-SCALE COMPREHENSIVE INITIATIVE IS TO RESTORE CONNECTIONS WITH TEXAS GRASSLANDS THROUGH RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND OUTREACH ACTIVITIES. ALONG WITH LAND-COVER CHANGES, THE SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS REGION IS UNDERGOING CULTURAL CHANGES, INCLUDING SHIFTS IN POPULATION DEMOGRAPHICS AND LANDOWNER PRIORITIES. TO ADDRESS THESE REGIONAL CHANGES IN LAND-COVER AND STAKEHOLDER DEMOGRAPHICS AND VALUES, TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY PROPOSES A LARGE-SCALE, COMPREHENSIVE RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND OUTREACH CAPACITY-BUILDING INITIATIVE FOCUSED ON VITAL GRASSLAND ECOSYSTEMS AND THEIR BENEFITS TO SOCIETY. THE RESTORE TEXAS GRASSLAND REVITALIZATION PARTNERSHIP WILL BE A BASIC AND APPLIED LAND MANAGEMENT PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY, TEXAS A&M AGRILIFE RESEARCH, AND THE BOTANICAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF TEXAS THAT INTEGRATES STUDENT PARTICIPATION IN DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING INNOVATIVE APPROACHES TO GRASSLAND RESTORATION, LAND MANAGEMENT, AND CONSERVATION IN A COORDINATED PROGRAM CENTERED ON MEETING CRITICAL NEEDS OF LANDOWNERS WHILE MAXIMIZING ECOSYSTEM SERVICES TO URBAN AND RURAL AREAS.GRASSLAND RESEARCH PROJECTS ADDRESS THE SYNERGISTIC THEMES OF WOODY PLANT EXPANSION, WATER RESOURCES, AND SOIL HEALTH, WHICH HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED AS TOP PRIORITIES OF LANDOWNERS AND GRASSLAND MANAGERS IN NORTH-CENTRAL TEXAS. RESEARCH FINDINGS AND APPLICATIONS WILL BE CONVEYED THROUGH LANDOWNER NATURAL RESOURCE OUTREACH EVENTS. THIS PARTNERSHIP ADDRESSES THE NEED FOR INCREASED STUDENT RECRUITMENT, EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING, AND LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT THROUGH PARTICIPATION IN UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH EXPERIENCES, INTERNSHIPS, AND EXPANDED FIELD-BASED EXERCISES IN EXISTING TARLETON COURSES. THIS PROGRAM WILL LEVERAGE AND EXPAND ONGOING GRASSLAND RESEARCH AND OUTREACH BY FACILITATING AND ORGANIZING COMMUNICATION AND COORDINATION AMONG PARTNERS WHILE INCREASING THE CAPACITY OF TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY TO RECRUIT, RETAIN, AND EDUCATE A DIVERSE POPULATION OF GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS.

THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE NEED AREAS OF EDUCATION AND RESEARCH BY BUILDING ANAEROBIC DIGESTION CAPACITY TO INTEGRATE STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND CAREER PREPARATION WITH EXPERIMENTATION TO ENHANCE SUSTAINABLE AND RENEWABLE ENERGY DISCOVERY. IN CONTRAST TO THE GROWING NEED FOR TRAINED AND SKILLED WORKERS ENTERING THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES, THERE ARE INCREASING NUMBERS OF UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WHO ENROLL IN 4-YEAR BACHELORETTE AGRICULTURAL OR LIFE SCIENCES PROGRAMS WITHOUT PRIOR AGRICULTURAL WORK EXPERIENCE. INTRODUCTORY AGRICULTURAL COURSES AT ILLINOIS STATE UNIVERSITY ARE MADE UP OF 38.1% STUDENTS FROM AN URBAN CITY OR SUBURBAN AREA. ANAEROBIC DIGESTION CAN BE AN IMPORTANT COMPONENT OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL WASTE, NUTRIENT CYCLING, AND ENERGY MANAGEMENT, BUT THE COMPLEXITY OF THIS TECHNOLOGY AND PROCESS REQUIRES STUDENT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING TO DEVELOP USEFUL SKILL SETS AND THIS IS LACKING IN CENTRAL ILLINOIS. EDUCATION NEED AREAS OF PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTATION FOR EDUCATION AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING WILL BE ACHIEVED THROUGH THE EDUCATION TASK OBJECTIVES: 1) INCREASING UNDERGRADUATE PARTICIPATION AND TRAINING IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE RESEARCH; AND 2) ENHANCING TEACHING OF LABORATORY-BASED, HANDS-ON SKILLS ON ANAEROBIC DIGESTION. RESEARCH NEED AREAS WILL BE ADDRESSED BY: 1) DETERMINING POTENTIAL SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS OF COMBINING ANAEROBIC DIGESTION AND COMPOSTING FOR AGRICULTURAL WASTE MANAGEMENT; 2) QUANTIFYING THE REVENUES AND COSTS OF ADDING AN ANAEROBIC DIGESTION SYSTEM TO THE ILLINOIS STATE UNIVERSITY FARM AT LEXINGTON AND A LOCAL ORGANIC FARM TO IMPROVE WASTE, NUTRIENT, AND ENERGY MANAGEMENT; AND 3) EXAMINING AN BIO-ELECTROCHEMICAL METHOD FOR PHOSPHORUS RECOVERY FROM THE ANAEROBIC DIGESTION EFFLUENT.

EXAMPLES INCLUDE LOCAL FARMER-LED WATERSHED GROUPS (LAFAYETTE AG STEWARDSHIP ALLIANCE AND THE SOIL AND WATER HEALTH COALITION), NATIONAL FARMER-LED DAIRY SUSTAINABILITY EFFORTS (NET ZERO INITIATIVE), CONTINENTAL AND GLOBAL RESEARCH NETWORKS (USDA-ARS LONG-TERM AGRO-ECOSYSTEMS RESEARCH NETWORK AND TH GLOBAL FARM PLATFORM).THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSED RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND OUTREACH PROJECT IS TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECTS OF THREE DAIRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS (CONFINED DAIRY WITH CONVENTIONAL TILL CROP PRODUCTION, CONFINED DAIRY WITH NO-TILL CROP PRODUCTION, AND HYBRID GRAZED DAIRY) ON WATER QUALITY AND NUTRIENT CYCLING. ULTIMATELY, WE SEE THIS PROJECT AS A VESSEL TO DEVELOP MEANINGFUL, INTEGRATED, ENVIRONMENTAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL INSTRUMENTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF LONG-TERM IMPROVED LAND AND WATER RESOURCE USE AT THE CATCHMENT, REGIONAL, CONTINENTAL, AND GLOBAL SCALE.TO SUPPORT OUR GOALS WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING SUPPORTING OBJECTIVES: I) EXTEND RESEARCH CAPACITY OF PIONEER FARM GREENHOUSE GAS MONITORING TO INCLUDE CH4, N2O, AND NH3; II) INSTALL LYSIMETERS WITHIN PERENNIAL PASTURES TO COMPLEMENT VADOSE ZONE LEACHING MONITORING CURRENTLY CONDUCTED IN AGRONOMIC FIELDS, III) INVESTIGATE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DAIRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND SURFACE-WATER CONTAMINATION (SOIL LOSS, NITROGEN, PHOSPHORUS), GROUNDWATER CONTAMINATION (BACTERIAL, NITRATE), AND GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS (CO2, CH4, N2O, AND NH3); IV) DEVELOP AN INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCHERS TO PARTICIPATE IN RESEARCH ACTIVITIES; AND V) COMMUNICATE PROJECT RESULTS TO STAKEHOLDERS VIA THE NET ZERO, GLOBAL FARM PLATFORM, AND USDA LONG TERM AGROECOSYSTEM RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE PARTNERSHIPS.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS INTEGRATED PROJECT IS TO BUILD CAPACITY FOR FORAGE AND ANIMAL SCIENCE (A AND P CODES) PROGRAMS THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FUNCTIONAL FORAGE NUTRITION LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF TENNESSEE AT MARTIN IN COLLABORATION WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI. THIS ACCOMPLISHES SUPPORTING OBJECTIVES TO STRENGTHEN UG TEACHING TO ENHANCE STUDENT LEARNING, INCREASE YOUTH PARTICIPATION IN AGRICULTURE AND, SUPPORT LIVESTOCK COMMUNITIES IN DEVELOPING SUMMER FORAGE MANAGEMENT SKILLS THROUGH RESEARCH AND OUTREACH ACTIVITIES. UNDER OUTREACH, THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THE NEED AREAS OF 4-H ACTIVITY AND FANH SCIENCES. positiveFlows.title: COMMUNITIES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES RELY ON LAND APPLICATION OF BIOSOLIDS AS A COST?EFFECTIVE WAY TO RECYCLE NUTRIENTS, SUPPORT CROP PRODUCTION, AND REDUCE LANDFILLING. HOWEVER, GROWING EVIDENCE SHOWS THAT BIOSOLIDS MAY CONTAIN PFAS (POPULARLY CALLED FOREVER CHEMICALS) THAT, IF RELEASED INTO THE SOIL ENVIRONMENT, CAN MOVE THROUGH SOIL INTO GROUNDWATER AND CROPS, AND EVENTUALLY INTO THE FOOD CHAIN. THIS ISSUE EXTENDS BEYOND FARMERS AND WASTEWATER UTILITIES, AS PFAS CONTAMINATION AFFECTS DRINKING WATER, PUBLIC HEALTH, FARM ECONOMIES, REGULATORY COSTS, AND TRUST IN EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT WASTE?REUSE PRACTICES. TO ADDRESS THIS CHALLENGE, THE PROJECT WILL EVALUATE PRACTICAL SOIL TREATMENT APPROACHES THAT USE BIOCHAR (A CHARCOAL?LIKE MATERIAL MADE FROM AGRICULTURAL AND WASTEWATER BYPRODUCTS) TO BIND PFAS AND KEEP THEM FROM MOVING INTO WATER OR PLANTS. RESEARCHERS WILL CONDUCT CONTROLLED LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS AND REAL?WORLD FIELD TRIALS TO MEASURE HOW WELL DIFFERENT BIOCHAR MATERIALS REDUCE PFAS MOVEMENT IN SOIL, WHILE WORKING CLOSELY WITH EXTENSION SPECIALISTS AND STAKEHOLDERS TO TRANSLATE RESULTS INTO USABLE GUIDANCE. THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP AFFORDABLE, FIELD?TESTED SOLUTIONS THAT ALLOW COMMUNITIES TO CONTINUE BENEFITING FROM BIOSOLIDS REUSE WHILE REDUCING RISKS TO WATER QUALITY, FOOD SYSTEMS, AND HUMAN HEALTH. IF SUCCESSFUL, THE PROJECT WILL SUPPORT SAFER FARMING PRACTICES, PROTECT DRINKING WATER RESOURCES, STRENGTHEN RURAL AND MUNICIPAL ECONOMIES, AND PROVIDE SCIENCE?BASED TOOLS THAT HELP COMMUNITIES ADAPT TO EMERGING PFAS REGULATIONS.

A SKILLED WORKFORCE IS NEEDED TO SUPPORT SAFE, RELIABLE, AND HEALTH-PROMOTING FOOD SYSTEMS. MANY PROGRAMS ALSO NEED MORE HANDS-ON TRAINING CAPACITY THAT CONNECTS CLASSROOM LEARNING TO REAL-WORLD FOOD PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, AND SAFETY CHALLENGES. THIS PROJECT STRENGTHENS EDUCATION AND RESEARCH CAPACITY IN FOOD, NUTRITION, AND HEALTH SCIENCES BY UPGRADING TEACHING LABORATORIES AND EXPANDING STRUCTURED TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY, FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY, AND THE USDA HEALTHY PROCESSED FOODS RESEARCH UNIT.THE PROJECT WILL MODERNIZE A TEACHING LABORATORY WITH UPDATED EQUIPMENT AND PROVIDE SUPERVISED RESEARCH EXPERIENCES AND INTERNSHIPS THAT BUILD PRACTICAL SKILLS IN FOOD SUSTAINABILITY AND FOOD SAFETY. STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN LABORATORY PROJECTS AND INTERNSHIPS FOCUSED ON TOPICS SUCH AS TRANSFORMING FRUIT BYPRODUCTS INTO DIETARY FIBER INGREDIENTS AND EVALUATING APPROACHES TO REDUCE FOOD SAFETY RISKS IN LEAFY GREENS SYSTEMS. RESULTS WILL BE SHARED THROUGH PRESENTATIONS, REPORTS, AND PROJECT ACTIVITIES THAT SUPPORT TRAINING AND BROADER ENGAGEMENT.

CORN IS ONE OF AMERICA'S MOST IMPORTANT CROPS, SUPPORTING FOOD PRODUCTION, LIVESTOCK FEED, AND BIOFUEL INDUSTRIES. MUCH OF WHAT DETERMINES A CORN PLANT'S STRENGTH AND PRODUCTIVITY HAPPENS UNDERGROUND IN ITS ROOT SYSTEM, YET ROOTS ARE DIFFICULT TO STUDY. CURRENT METHODS FOR MEASURING ROOT TRAITS ARE SLOW, LABOR-INTENSIVE, AND OFTEN SUBJECTIVE, CREATING BOTTLENECKS IN CROP BREEDING. WEAK ROOT SYSTEMS CAN CAUSE PLANTS TO FALL OVER (A PROBLEM KNOWN AS LODGING), LEADING TO REDUCED YIELDS AND HARVEST CHALLENGES. IMPROVING HOW WE MEASURE AND UNDERSTAND ROOT SYSTEMS IS ESSENTIAL FOR INCREASING FARM PRODUCTIVITY, STRENGTHENING RURAL ECONOMIES, AND ENSURING RELIABLE FOOD PRODUCTION.THIS PROJECT WILL MODERNIZE ROOT MEASUREMENT BY DEVELOPING HIGH-THROUGHPUT IMAGING AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TOOLS TO ANALYZE CORN ROOTS QUICKLY AND OBJECTIVELY. RESEARCHERS WILL COLLECT DETAILED IMAGES OF FIELD-GROWN ROOTS AND USE COMPUTER-BASED ANALYSIS TO MEASURE ROOT STRENGTH, STRUCTURE, AND ORIENTATION. ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WILL HELP UNCOVER PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN ROOT CHARACTERISTICS LINKED TO PLANT PERFORMANCE. A NEW NON-INVASIVE 3D IMAGING METHOD WILL DIGITALLY RECONSTRUCT ROOT SYSTEMS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THEIR ARCHITECTURE WITHOUT DAMAGING THE PLANT. BY PROVIDING BREEDERS WITH FASTER AND MORE PRECISE TOOLS TO EVALUATE ROOT SYSTEMS, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ACCELERATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF STRONGER, MORE PRODUCTIVE CORN VARIETIES. THE RESEARCH WILL ALSO TRAIN STUDENTS IN ADVANCED AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGIES, STRENGTHENING RESEARCH CAPACITY AND PREPARING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL ENGINEERS AND SCIENTISTS.

IN SEMI-ARID REGIONS, ACHIEVING SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTIVITY HINGES ON IMPROVING WATER USE EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVING SCARCE WATER RESOURCES. EFFECTIVE IRRIGATION MANAGEMENT IS ESSENTIAL, YET CHALLENGING, DUE TO THE DIFFICULTY OF ACCURATELY ASSESSING CROP WATER STRESS UNDER FLUCTUATING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. HIGH-THROUGHPUT PLANT PHENOTYPING, ENHANCED BY REMOTE SENSING, ADVANCED DATA SCIENCE, AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI), PROVIDES A PROMISING PATHWAY TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES. BY ENABLING PRECISE, SCALABLE WATER STRESS ASSESSMENTS AT MULTIPLE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL SCALES, THESE TECHNOLOGIES CAN SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE WATER CONSERVATION EFFORTS.THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH A HIGH-THROUGHPUT PHENOTYPING FRAMEWORK THAT SUPPORTS SUSTAINABLE WATER USE STRATEGIES FOR CROPS GROWN UNDER LIMITED WATER CONDITIONS. THIS FRAMEWORK WILL CONSIST OF STANDARDIZED PROTOCOLS FOR DATA COLLECTION ACROSS SCALES, INTEGRATED WITH AI AND CROP MODELS TO QUANTIFY AND PREDICT CROP GROWTH AND WATER STRESS. OUR SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES INCLUDE: (1) DEVELOPING A STANDARDIZED PROTOCOL FOR THE COLLECTION, PROCESSING, AND ORGANIZATION OF MULTI-SCALE DATA ON CROP WATER STRESS, (2) CREATING MACHINE LEARNING MODELS TO PREDICT CROP GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT UNDER VARYING WATER STRESS CONDITIONS, AND (3) BUILDING A TOOL THAT COMBINES MACHINE LEARNING AND CROP MODELS TO OFFER REAL-TIME, ACTIONABLE INSIGHTS FOR IRRIGATION MANAGEMENT.BY ESTABLISHING THIS FRAMEWORK, WE AIM TO PROVIDE FARMERS AND STAKEHOLDERS WITH ROBUST, DATA-DRIVEN TOOLS THAT SUPPORT INFORMED, TIMELY IRRIGATION DECISIONS. THE ANTICIPATED IMPACT INCLUDES IMPROVED WATER USE EFFICIENCY, ENHANCED CROP RESILIENCE, AND A REPLICABLE MODEL FOR PRECISION WATER MANAGEMENT. THIS PROJECT ALIGNS WITH BROADER SUSTAINABILITY GOALS, AIMING TO SAFEGUARD PRODUCTIVITY IN WATER-LIMITED AGRICULTURAL REGIONS.

THIS PROJECT WILL BUILD U.S. RESEARCH AND WORKFORCE CAPACITY AT TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY TO BETTER UNDERSTAND AND MANAGE WOODY PLANT COVER CHANGE IN TEXAS SAVANNA-GRASSLAND WORKING LANDS. WOODY ENCROACHMENT AFFECTS FORAGE AVAILABILITY, BIODIVERSITY, AND LAND MANAGEMENT OUTCOMES ACROSS MANY TEXAS RANGELANDS. THE PROJECT WILL GENERATE NEW BASELINE FIELD DATA ON WOODY COVER, PLANT VARIETY, AND PRODUCTIVITY AND WILL INTEGRATE THOSE DATA WITH SATELLITE AND GIS ANALYSES OF WOODY COVER CHANGE AND KEY DRIVERS OVER THE LAST 20 YEARS. PROJECT-GENERATED DATASETS WILL BE SHARED THROUGH USDA'S AG DATA COMMONS WITH APPROPRIATE PRIVACY PROTECTIONS.EDUCATION ACTIVITIES WILL STRENGTHEN U.S. TRAINING BY INTEGRATING PROJECT-BASED LEARNING INTO EXISTING COURSES, SUPPORTING UNDERGRADUATE APPLIED LEARNING EXPERIENCES AND GRADUATE RESEARCH TRAINING, AND PRODUCING STUDENT RESEARCH PRODUCTS AND PRESENTATIONS. THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE IMPROVED BASELINE INFORMATION AND DECISION SUPPORT FOR TEXAS WORKING LANDS MANAGEMENT, STRENGTHENED LONG-TERM RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CAPACITY AT TARLETON STATE UNIVERSITY, AND A BETTER-PREPARED NATURAL RESOURCES WORKFORCE TO SUPPORT U.S. AGRICULTURE AND RURAL COMMUNITIES.INTERNATIONAL COLLABORATION ACTIVITIES, WHERE USED, WILL BE LIMITED AND WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT U.S. PROJECT OBJECTIVES BY PROVIDING COMPARATIVE CONTEXT AND METHODOLOGICAL INSIGHT THAT IMPROVES INTERPRETATION OF TEXAS RESULTS AND EXPANDS THE EVIDENCE BASE FOR U.S.-RELEVANT SAVANNA RANGELAND MANAGEMENT. THE PROJECT DOES NOT PROPOSE REGULATORY ADVOCACY AND WILL BE IMPLEMENTED CONSISTENT WITH APPLICABLE LAW AND SUBJECT TO THE AVAILABILITY OF APPROPRIATIONS.

FOODBORNE ILLNESS LINKED TO FRESH PRODUCE IS A PERSISTENT PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGE IN THE UNITED STATES. SALMONELLA ENTERICA ALONE CAUSES OVER 1.35 MILLION INFECTIONS ANNUALLY, WITH A SUBSTANTIAL SHARE ATTRIBUTED TO CONTAMINATED FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. CONVENTIONAL PATHOGEN DETECTION METHODS ARE EFFECTIVE FOR KNOWN STRAINS BUT FREQUENTLY FAIL TO IDENTIFY STRESSED OR EMERGING THREATS WITHIN THE COMPLEX MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES FOUND ON FRESH PRODUCE. REGIONAL WEATHER PATTERNS AND AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES ADD FURTHER VARIABILITY, LIMITING THE RELIABILITY OF STANDARD FOOD SAFETY PROTOCOLS ACROSS PRODUCTION ENVIRONMENTS. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THESE GAPS BY APPLYING METAGENOMICS A DNA-BASED TECHNOLOGY THAT ANALYZES ALL MICROBIAL LIFE IN A SAMPLE SIMULTANEOUSLY TO FRESH SPINACH AT MULTIPLE POINTS ALONG THE PRODUCTION CHAIN. THE RESEARCH WILL CHARACTERIZE HOW NATIVE MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES INTERACT WITH SALMONELLA, ASSESS HOW TEMPERATURE AND HUMIDITY FLUCTUATIONS DURING STORAGE AND TRANSPORT AFFECT PATHOGEN SURVIVAL, AND USE THESE FINDINGS TO DEVELOP PRACTICAL GUIDANCE FOR GROWERS, PACKERS, AND FOOD SAFETY PROFESSIONALS. BEYOND THE LABORATORY, THE PROJECT WILL TRAIN THE NEXT GENERATION OF FOOD SAFETY SCIENTISTS THROUGH HANDS-ON RESEARCH EXPERIENCE, EQUIPPING STUDENTS WITH HIGH-DEMAND TECHNICAL SKILLS IN METAGENOMICS AND MICROBIAL ANALYSIS. OUTCOMES WILL STRENGTHEN PRODUCE SAFETY SYSTEMS, IMPROVE COLD CHAIN MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, AND EXPAND THE NATION'S TECHNICALLY SKILLED FOOD SAFETY WORKFORCE.
