positiveFlows.title: TO ENSURE GRADUATES ARE FULLY PREPARED FOR THE WORKFORCE, MSUVTP MUST KEEP UP WITH MODERN VETERINARY PRACTICES AND EQUIPMENT. THE PROGRAM CURRENTLY LACKS SUFFICIENT FUNDING TO PURCHASE UPDATED TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY, WHICH LIMITS STUDENTS' OPPORTUNITIES TO PRACTICE IMPORTANT CLINICAL SKILLS. THIS GRANT WOULD PROVIDE CRITICAL EQUIPMENT THAT SUPPORTS HIGH-QUALITY, REAL-WORLD TRAINING.THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON SEVERAL MAIN SKILL AREAS ESSENTIAL IN TODAY'S VETERINARY FIELD: ALTERNATIVE THERAPEUTICS, GENETIC IMPROVEMENT, DISEASE DIAGNOSIS, AND TREATMENT FOR BOTH SMALL AND LARGE ANIMALS.THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE PREPARATION OF UP TO 40 STUDENTS EACH YEAR, HELPING THEM ENTER THE WORKFORCE WITH ADVANCED, JOB-READY SKILLS. ANIMALS TREATED IN THE TEACHING HOSPITAL WILL RECEIVE BETTER CARE, AND REGIONAL VETERINARY PRACTICES WILL BENEFIT FROM HIGHLY TRAINED GRADUATES WHO CAN HELP MEET THE GROWING DEMAND FOR VETERINARY SERVICES IN BOTH THE SMALL ANIMAL AND LARGE ANIMAL SECTORS.

THIS PROJECT SEEKS FUNDING TO SUPPORT THE INCLUSION OF STUDENTS ENROLLED IN SEVERAL COURSES INTO AN ONGOING, LONG-TERM RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROJECT FOCUSED ON THE IMPACTS OF TILE DRAINAGE ON WATER QUALITY AND SOIL HEALTH AND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF CONTROLLED TILE DRAINAGE ON MITIGATING THOSE IMPACTS. THIS PROJECT WOULD PROVIDE A DIVERSE MIX OF STUDENTS, RANGING FROM FRESHMEN TO GRADUATE ACROSS SEVERAL MAJORS, WITH HIGH-IMPACT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING. THE PROJECT IS PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON EDUCATION BUT INCLUDES RESEARCH AND OUTREACH. FUNDING IS REQUESTED TO ACQUIRE EQUIPMENT FOR STUDENT USE, COVER TRAVEL EXPENSES FOR STUDENTS TO AN EXPERIMENTAL AND DEMONSTRATION FARM APPROXIMATELY 20 MILES FROM CAMPUS, AND SUPPORT A GRADUATE ASSISTANT FOR THREE YEARS.THE PROJECT IS WITHIN ACADEMIC CODES D (SOIL SCIENCE) AND C (CONSERVATION AND RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES) AND MEETS SEVERAL EDUCATION NEED AREAS, INCLUDING CURRICULUM DESIGN/MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT (DESIGNING TWO OPEN-SOURCE LABORATORY MANUALS THAT INCORPORATE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING); SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTATION (ACQUIRING SCIENTIFIC INSTRUMENTATION FOR STUDENT USE); AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING (INCORPORATING STUDENTS INTO FIELD AND LABORATORY RESEARCH AND OUTREACH). STUDENTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO RESEARCH NEED AREAS, INCLUDING STUDIES AND EXPERIMENTATION AND APPLIED STUDIES IN THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (PARTICIPATING IN AND SHARING RESULTS OF SYSTEMS-ORIENTED AND COMMUNITY-BASED RESEARCH). STUDENTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO OUTREACH/EXTENSION NEED AREAS, INCLUDING FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (ASSISTING FARMERS TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY THROUGH SOUND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES), LEADERSHIP DEVELOPMENT (TRAINING STUDENTS AND ENCOURAGING INVOLVEMENT AND LEADERSHIP ROLES WITHIN THE AGRICULTURE COMMUNITY), AND NATURAL RESOURCES (INFORMING LANDOWNERS, CONSULTANTS, AND CONSERVATIONISTS TO USE NATURAL RESOURCES WISELY AND PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT).

REGIONALLY SUITABLE GRAPE CULTIVARS ARE NEEDED. KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS OF PLANT GENETICS AND BIOTECHNOLOGY ARE LESS AVAILABLE TO STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURE-CONCENTRATED REGIONS. THIS PROJECT INTEGRATES PLANT BREEDING WITH IMPACTFUL EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAMS. WE WILL ACHIEVE TWO GOALS: 1) EDUCATE AND TRAIN STUDENTS WITH KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS IN PLANT GENETICS AND BIOTECHNOLOGY; 2) BUILD GENETIC RESOURCES FOR BREEDING REGIONALLY ADAPTED NEW GRAPE CULTIVARS.THE PROJECT FULFILLS THE MISSION OF RESEARCH AND EDUCATION IN CODE P: PLANT SCIENCES AND HORTICULTURE. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THREE OBJECTIVES: 1) PHENOTYPE A SELF-FERTILIZED NORTON POPULATION (SFNP) OF 300 SEEDLINGS FOR DISEASE RESISTANCE; 2) PHENOTYPE SFNP FOR SENSITIVITY TO SULFUR-BASED FUNGICIDES; 3) EXTRACT GENOMIC DNA FROM 300 SEEDLINGS. IN THE EDUCATION COMPONENT, WE WILL EDUCATE AND TRAIN 36 HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, 6 UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, AND ONE GRADUATE STUDENT IN PLANT SCIENCE. WE WILL REPORT ON VITICULTURALLY IMPORTANT TRAITS OF THE 300 GRAPEVINES: DISEASE RESISTANCE TO TWO DESTRUCTIVE FUNGAL PATHOGENS AND GRAPEVINE VEIN CLEARING VIRUS, AND FUNGICIDE SENSITIVITY. WE WILL REPORT THE OUTCOMES OF EDUCATING AND TRAINING STUDENTS FOR GAINING COLLEGE AND POSTGRADUATE DEGREES AND FOR PROFESSIONAL PLACEMENT.

WITH RISING PREVALENCE OF GUT HEALTH DISORDERS, THERE IS A NEED TO DEVELOP FUNCTIONAL FOODS THAT SUPPORT DIGESTIVE HEALTH. THIS RESEARCH EXPLORES THE POTENTIAL OF PULSE-BASED YOGURT AS A FUNCTIONAL PLANT-BASED DAIRY ALTERNATIVE THAT MAY SUPPORT GUT HEALTH. PULSES ARE RICH IN PROTEIN, FIBER, AND SERVE AS A GOOD SOURCE OF VITAMINS AND MINERALS, SUCH AS IRON, MAGNESIUM, FOLIC ACID, AND ZINC. AS DIETARY TRENDS SHIFT TOWARDS VEGAN AND LACTOSE-FREE PRODUCTS DUE TO LIFESTYLE CHOICES AND MEDICAL CONDITIONS LIKE LACTOSE INTOLERANCE, CHOLESTEROL CONCERNS, DAIRY ALLERGIES, AND GUT MICROBIOME IMBALANCE, DEMAND FOR PLANT-BASED DAIRY ALTERNATIVES CONTINUE TO RISE. THIS STUDY AIMS TO ADDRESS THIS NEED BY FORMULATING PULSE-BASED YOGURT AND EVALUATING ITS MICROBIAL AND NUTRITIONAL CHARACTERISTICS. SPECIFICALLY, IT WILL EVALUATE THE VIABILITY OF BENEFICIAL GUT BACTERIA IN PULSE-BASED YOGURT COMPARED TO TRADITIONAL PLANT-BASED YOGURTS. THE STUDY WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE SURVIVAL OF BENEFICIAL BACTERIA IN THE YOGURT IN SIMULATED IN-VITRO GASTROINTESTINAL (GI) CONDITIONS. BY MEASURING THE BACTERIAL VIABILITY AND SURVIVAL, THE STUDY WILL PROVIDE INSIGHTS WHETHER PULSE-BASED YOGURT CAN MAINTAIN PROBIOTIC ACTIVITY COMPARABLE TO TRADITIONAL YOGURTS. ADDITIONALLY, THE RESEARCH EXPLORES THE ANTAGONISTIC ACTIVITY OF PULSE-BASED YOGURT AGAINST HARMFUL PATHOGENS. THIS RESEARCH EXPLORES PULSE'S ROLE IN SUPPORTING GUT HEALTH THROUGH THEIR PROBIOTIC AND PREBIOTIC PROPERTIES, WHICH ARE CURRENTLY NOT WELL UNDERSTOOD. PRELIMINARY DATA COLLECTED WILL INFORM FUTURE RESEARCH ON OPTIMIZING PULSE-BASED YOGURT FOR MAXIMUM HEALTH BENEFITS AND FUNCTIONALITY. ULTIMATELY, THESE FINDINGS AIM TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF HIGH-QUALITY PLANT-BASED YOGURTS THAT MEET DIETARY NEEDS OF CONSUMERS SEEKING GUT-HEALTH SUPPORTIVE FOOD OPTIONS.

THE ET AT ET PROJECT USED PERENNIAL GARDENS ON THE EAST TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY FARM TO EXPLORE THE USE OF A NEW PIECE OF EQUIPMENT TO MEASURE EVAPOTRANSPIRATION (ET) AND COMPARE ITS USE TO OTHER CURRENT TECHNIQUES TO PROVIDE IRRIGATION TO BEDS CONTAINING HERBACEOUS PERENNIALS.CURRENTLY, LANDSCAPERS ACROSS NORTH CENTRAL AND NORTHEAST TEXAS ARE GIVEN A RECOMMENDATION OF PROVIDING ONE INCH OF IRRIGATION TO OUR LANDSCAPES. HOWEVER, USING ET, WHICH COMBINES THE WATER LOST FROM THE SOIL SURFACE (EVAPORATION) WITH THE WATER LOST FROM PLANT LEAVES (TRANSPIRATION). TOGETHER, THESE TELL US HOW MUCH WATER OUR PLANTS ARE USING. IF WE CAN FIND THIS AMOUNT, WE CAN ACCURATELY APPLY ONLY THE WATER OUR PLANTS NEED TO GROW. THIS AMOUNT IS VERY OFTEN WELL BELOW THE ONE INCH OF IRRIGATION RECOMMENDED.IN OUR PROJECT, WE WILL USE AN ET NODE. THIS IS A RELATIVELY NEW PIECE OF EQUIPMENT AVAILABLE FROM LICOR, A COMPANY KNOWN FOR HIGH QUALITY ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING EQUIPMENT. TODAY, WE ESTIMATE ET USING THE PENMAN-MONTIETH EQUATION, A FORMULA THAT USES WEATHER VARIABLES, SUCH AS SUNLIGHT, TEMPERATURE, RELATIVE HUMIDITY, AND WIND. THE ACCURACY OF THE EQUATION IS RELATED TO THE QUALITY OF THE WEATHER STATION AND THE RELATIVE LOCATION TO THE STUDY SITE.OUR STUDY WILL EVALUATE GROWTH OF PERENNIALS IRRIGATED AT ET, MINUS A PLANT COEFFICIENT OF 0.5 (RECOMMENDED FOR HERBACEOUS PERENNIALS) AND A PLANT QUALITY FACTOR OF 0.6 (WHICH REPRESENTS NORMAL PLANT QUALITY). THE ADJUSTMENTS ARE CONSISTENT WITH THOSE RECOMMENDED BY TEXAS A&M AGRILIFE FOR HERBACEOUS PERENNIALS GROWN IN OUR AREA. OUR ET WILL VARY ACCORDING TO MEASUREMENTS TAKEN BY THE ET NODE IMMEDIATELY ON SITE, CALCULATED ET FROM A WEATHER STATION, APPROXIMATELY 500 M FROM THE STUDY SITE, AND FROM A TEXAS A&M AGRILIFE ET NETWORK STATION 32 KM FROM THE STUDY SITE.WE WILL EVALUATE THE PLANTS BASED ON PLANT PERFORMANCE (BLOOM NUMBER, FOLIAGE QUALITY, PLANT FORM) AND NUMBER OF POLLINATOR VISITS. PLANTS WILL BE EVALUATED WEEKLY, AND WE WILL BE ABLE TO DEVELOP A STRONG UNDERSTANDING OF THE SPECIES THAT PERFORM WELL UNDER THIS IRRIGATION REGIME, WHICH MAINTAIN A HEALTHY OPPORTUNITY FOR POLLINATOR FORAGING, AND WHICH TECHNIQUE PROVIDES THE MOST ACCURATE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR IRRIGATION NEEDS ON A WEEKLY BASIS.THE INFORMATION COLLECTED WILL BE TAUGHT TO OUR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, SO THEY HAVE A KEEN UNDERSTANDING OF PLANT IRRIGATION NEEDS. STUDENTS WILL ALSO UNDERSTAND HOW CLOSELY OUR ET AND IRRIGATION RECOMMENDATIONS ARE RELATED. THEY WILL ALSO UNDERSTAND HOW USING ACCURATE INFORMATION, ALLOWS US TO USE A SCARCE RESOURCE WISELY AND IN A WAY THAT MAINTAINS OUR GARDENS.

HYDROPONIC PRODUCTION SYSTEMS (HPSS) ARE EXPANDING RAPIDLY AS GROWERS SEEK STABLE, HIGH-YIELD PRODUCTION METHODS THAT REDUCE LAND REQUIREMENTS AND IMPROVE WATER EFFICIENCY. BY 2028, HYDROPONIC ACREAGE IS PROJECTED TO INCREASE SUBSTANTIALLY. IN 2020, U.S. TOMATO PRODUCTION WAS VALUED AT APPROXIMATELY $2 BILLION, WITH MORE THAN HALF OF PRODUCTION OCCURRING IN HYDROPONIC SYSTEMS. AS ADOPTION INCREASES, IMPROVING NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT EFFICIENCY WITHIN THESE SYSTEMS BECOMES CRITICAL TO MAINTAINING PROFITABILITY AND LONG-TERM VIABILITY.WHILE HYDROPONICS ALLOWS FOR PRECISE DELIVERY OF WATER AND NUTRIENTS, NUTRIENT-RICH DISCHARGE SOLUTIONS CAN ACCUMULATE OVER TIME. IF NOT PROPERLY MANAGED, THESE SOLUTIONS REPRESENT BOTH LOST FERTILIZER INVESTMENT AND POTENTIAL NUTRIENT MOVEMENT INTO NEARBY WATER SYSTEMS. FERTILIZER INPUTS ARE AMONG THE HIGHEST RECURRING COSTS IN HYDROPONIC VEGETABLE PRODUCTION. EVEN SMALL IMPROVEMENTS IN NUTRIENT USE EFFICIENCY CAN TRANSLATE INTO MEASURABLE COST SAVINGS AT THE FARM LEVEL AND IMPROVED RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP AT THE REGIONAL SCALE.THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A PRACTICAL, DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-SUPPORT MODEL THAT HELPS PRODUCERS OPTIMIZE NUTRIENT REPLENISHMENT AND DISCHARGE MANAGEMENT IN HYDROPONIC TOMATO SYSTEMS. BY INTEGRATING MEASURABLE PRODUCTION VARIABLES SUCH AS LIGHT INTENSITY, VAPOR PRESSURE DEFICIT, AND PLANT WATER USE, THIS RESEARCH WILL IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING OF NUTRIENT UPTAKE DYNAMICS AND SOLUTION CONCENTRATION CHANGES OVER TIME.SPECIFICALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL:QUANTIFY HOW PRODUCTION-RELATED VARIABLES INFLUENCE NUTRIENT FATE AND DISTRIBUTION WITHIN HYDROPONIC FERTIGATION SYSTEMS;DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE MODEL OF PLANT TRANSPIRATION BASED ON VAPOR PRESSURE DEFICIT AND SOLAR RADIATION; ANDCONSTRUCT AND VALIDATE A PRODUCTION-SCALE MODEL CAPABLE OF ESTIMATING NUTRIENT CONCENTRATIONS IN DISCHARGE SOLUTIONS TO GUIDE REPLENISHMENT DECISIONS.THE RESULTING FRAMEWORK WILL PROVIDE GROWERS WITH ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS TO REDUCE FERTILIZER WASTE, IMPROVE NUTRIENT RECOVERY, AND INCREASE INPUT EFFICIENCY WITHOUT SACRIFICING YIELD OR CROP QUALITY. BY LOWERING INPUT COSTS AND IMPROVING SYSTEM PERFORMANCE, THIS WORK SUPPORTS THE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY AND COMPETITIVENESS OF SPECIALTY CROP PRODUCERS.THE LONG-TERM OUTCOME OF THIS RESEARCH WILL BE THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN OPEN-SOURCE, USER-FRIENDLY MOBILE APPLICATION THAT TRANSLATES SCIENTIFIC MODELING INTO ACCESSIBLE, REAL-TIME MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE. THIS TOOL WILL REDUCE BARRIERS TO ADOPTION, INCREASE PRODUCER CONFIDENCE IN NUTRIENT DECISION-MAKING, AND ENHANCE PROFITABILITY ACROSS A RAPIDLY GROWING SECTOR OF U.S. AGRICULTURE. RESULTS ARE EXPECTED TO BE TRANSFERABLE TO OTHER HYDROPONICALLY GROWN CROPS, FURTHER AMPLIFYING ECONOMIC IMPACT.

THE AGRICULTURAL FINANCE INDUSTRY FACES A SERIOUS SHORTAGE OF HIGHLY QUALIFIED GRADUATES TO SERVE AS THE FUTURE OF AGRICULTURAL FINANCE DELIVERY. AGRICULTURAL FINANCE CAN BE BROADLY DEFINED TO INCLUDE AGRICULTURAL BANKING, LENDING, AND CREDIT, INSURANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT, COMMODITY TRADING/MERCHANDISING, REAL ESTATE, AND WEALTH MANAGEMENT. THERE IS A GROWING NEED FOR GREATER SPECIALIZED TRAINING BECAUSE OF THE INCREASING COMPLEXITY OF AGRICULTURAL FINANCE. GENERAL BUSINESS-TRAINED GRADUATES ARE OFTEN UNPREPARED FOR AGRICULTURAL FINANCE BECAUSE THEY LACK AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE SPECIAL CHARACTERISTICS, INHERENT IDIOSYNCRATIC RISKS, AND BIOLOGICAL NATURE OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION. THIS PROJECT CREATES A CERTIFICATION PROGRAM, EXCELLENCE IN AGRICULTURAL FINANCE, WITHIN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL AND APPLIED ECONOMICS (AAEC) AT TEXAS TECH UNIVERSITY (TTU), WHICH IDENTIFIES AND CULTIVATES QUALIFIED STUDENTS AND DEVELOPS A PIPELINE OF HIGHLY TRAINED STUDENTS WITH SPECIFIC EXPERTISE IN AGRICULTURAL FINANCE.THROUGH THIS PROGRAM, WE WILL CREATE AN INDUSTRY-BASED ADVISORY BOARD TO GUIDE PROGRAMMATIC DESIGN, SKILLS IDENTIFICATION, AND PARTICIPATION IN STUDENT DEVELOPMENT. THIS BOARD WILL BE COMPRISED OF INDUSTRY LEADERS ACROSS THE ABOVE-DEFINED SCOPE OF AGRICULTURAL FINANCE. ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS WILL ASSIST IN IDENTIFYING KEY SKILLS AND NEEDS OF THE INDUSTRY. ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN THE PROGRAM THROUGH HOSTING STUDENTS FOR SHADOWING EXERCISES, INTERNSHIPS, AND PROGRAM ACTIVITIES SUCH AS ROUNDTABLE DISCUSSIONS, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND CONFERENCES. PARTICIPATION OF ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS IS CRITICAL TO PROGRAM SUCCESS. THE CONCEPT IS BOARD MEMBERS BUY-IN TO THE PROGRAM THROUGH THE CREATION OF SCHOLARSHIP ENDOWMENTS THAT WILL SUPPORT THE PROGRAM IN THE LONG-TERM.THE PROGRAM WILL FOCUS ON RECRUITING HIGHLY MOTIVATED FIRST- AND SECOND-YEAR STUDENTS WITH AN INTEREST IN AGRICULTURAL FINANCE. THESE INITIAL STUDENTS WILL COMPLETE A SHADOWING EXERCISE DURING THE FIRST SUMMER OF THEIR PROGRAM. THIS SHORT-TERM EXERCISE WILL ALLOW STUDENTS SOME EXPERIENCE WITH THE SCOPE OF ACTIVITIES IN THE AGRICULTURAL FINANCE SECTOR TO ASCERTAIN CONTINUED INTEREST. WHILE THESE STUDENTS WILL LACK SPECIALIZED TRAINING AT THAT POINT, FIRMS CAN EVALUATE STUDENTS ON THEIR INTELLECTUAL CURIOSITY, MOTIVATION, AND OTHER SOFT SKILLS THAT ARE INDICATORS OF FUTURE SUCCESS. FOLLOWING COMPLETION OF THEIR SHADOWING EXERCISE, STUDENTS WILL SUBMIT AN APPLICATION THAT INCLUDES A STATEMENT OF GOALS AND OBJECTIVES, PLANS, AND A REVIEW OF THEIR EXPERIENCES DURING THE SHADOWING EXERCISE. THESE APPLICATIONS WILL BE REVIEWED BY ADVISORY BOARD MEMBERS AND TTU AAEC FACULTY MEMBERS TO DETERMINE STUDENTS FOR FORMAL ACCEPTANCE INTO THE PROGRAM. SELECTED STUDENTS WILL THEN BE INTERVIEWED FOR AND PARTICIPATE IN DEFINED INTERNSHIPS WITH ADVISORY BOARD MEMBER FIRMS OR OTHER FIRMS AS MATCHING OPPORTUNITIES AND INTERESTS FIT. THE INTERNSHIP WILL BE CONDUCTED IN EITHER THE SECOND OR TH,IRD SUMMER OF THEIR PROGRAM, DEPENDING ON STUDENT SCHEDULING NEEDS. ADDITIONALLY, EVERY ACCEPTED STUDENT WILL COMPLETE A SERIES OF LEARNING MODULES THAT ARE DESIGNED AND DELIVERED BY INDUSTRY AND FACULTY ON SPECIFIC TOPICS, SUCH AS HOW TO READ AND INTERPRET CROP AND LIVESTOCK USDA AND INDUSTRY REPORTS, WHAT ARE THE COSTS AND BENEFITS OF INSURANCE IN BUSINESS PLANNING AND RISK MANAGEMENT, OR HOW TO TALK TO CLIENTS ABOUT THEIR FINANCIAL SITUATION. STUDENTS MUST ALSO PARTICIPATE IN ROUNDTABLE DISCUSSIONS, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND CONFERENCES PROVIDED BY THE PROGRAM. FINALLY, STUDENTS MUST SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETE REQUIRED PROGRAM COURSEWORK IN DATA ANALYSIS AND SPREADSHEET MODELING, AGRIBUSINESS FINANCIAL ANALYSIS, APPLIED RISK ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT, COMMODITY FUTURES TRADING AND ANALYSIS, PROPERTY APPRAISAL, AND AGRIBUSINESS ENTERPRISE MANAGEMENT. IN ADDITION TO THESE REQUIRED COURSES, STUDENTS WILL BE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO INCORPORATE STRATEGIC AGRIBUSINESS MANAGEMENT AND BUSINESS LAW, AGRICULTURAL LAW, OR REAL ESTATE LAW.UPON COMPLETION OF THE REQUIRED EXTERNAL ACTIVITIES (SHADOWING, INTERNSHIP, AND LEARNING MODULES), AND SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE DEFINED REQUIRED COURSES, STUDENTS WILL BE AWARDED AN EXCELLENCE IN AGRICULTURAL FINANCE CERTIFICATE IN ADDITION TO THEIR AWARDED DEGREE. TO BE SUCCESSFUL, STUDENTS MUST EARN A GRADE OF B OR BETTER IN ALL REQUIRED COURSES. ADDITIONALLY, TO MAINTAIN PROGRAM FINANCIAL SUPPORT, STUDENTS MUST MAINTAIN A 3.25 GPA.THE PROPOSED PROGRAM IS NECESSARILY DEFINED AS ELITE. THE PURPOSE IS NOT SIMPLY TO TRAIN STUDENTS WITH COURSEWORK, BUT TO COMPLEMENT COURSEWORK WITH HIGH IMPACT EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES, SUPPLEMENTAL SPECIALIZED LEARNING MODULES, AND CREATE A HIGH-VALUE SOCIAL NETWORK BETWEEN COOPERATING BUSINESSES, STUDENTS, AND FACULTY. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS GOAL THAT SERVES BOTH STUDENTS AND INDUSTRY, THE PROGRAM MUST BE HIGHLY SELECTIVE TO IDENTIFY STUDENTS WITH THE GREATEST INTERNAL MOTIVATION FOR SUCCESS AND MATCH THEM WITH ENGAGED INDUSTRY LEADERS AND FIRMS.THIS ULTIMATE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT INVOLVES THE CREATION OF THIS CERTIFICATE PROGRAM AND THE FIRST TWO YEARS OF OPERATION. FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR STUDENT STIPENDS/SCHOLARSHIPS, CREATION OF LEARNING MODULES, AND EXPENSES RELATED TO HOSTING ROUNDTABLES, SEMINARS, WORKSHOPS, AND CONFERENCES. THE PROGRAM WILL BECOME SELF-SUFFICIENT BY YEAR THREE AS EXTERNAL INDUSTRY-BASED ENDOWMENTS ARE BUILT, AND EARNINGS ARE GENERATED TO MAINTAIN LONG-TERM SUPPORT FOR STUDENT SCHOLARSHIPS AND PROGRAM OPERATIONS.

NON-TECHNICAL SUMMARYTHIS PLANNING GRANT WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A COLLABORATIVE 2+2+2 EDUCATIONAL PATHWAY IN FOOD SCIENCE TO STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE READINESS AND IMPROVE STRUCTURED TRANSFER OPPORTUNITIES ACROSS MASSACHUSETTS. FRAMINGHAM STATE UNIVERSITY (FSU) WILL CONVENE A WORKING GROUP OF SECONDARY SCHOOLS, COMMUNITY COLLEGES, AND INDUSTRY PARTNERS TO DESIGN A COORDINATED FRAMEWORK THAT ALIGNS CURRICULUM, DUAL ENROLLMENT OPPORTUNITIES, AND TRANSFER AGREEMENTS INTO FSU'S FOOD SCIENCE PROGRAM.MASSACHUSETTS HAS EXPANDED ACCESS TO COMMUNITY COLLEGE THROUGH TUITION-FREE INITIATIVES, CREATING AN OPPORTUNITY TO BUILD CLEARER PATHWAYS INTO HIGH-DEMAND AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SCIENCE CAREERS. HOWEVER, FOOD SCIENCE REMAINS A SPECIALIZED FIELD WITH LIMITED STRUCTURED TRANSFER ROUTES, PARTICULARLY FOR STUDENTS BEGINNING AT HIGH SCHOOLS, TECHNICAL SCHOOLS, OR TWO-YEAR INSTITUTIONS. THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY EXISTING STRENGTHS, ADDRESS CURRICULAR MISALIGNMENTS, AND DEVELOP A FRAMEWORK THAT SUPPORTS TIMELY PROGRESSION INTO A FOUR-YEAR FOOD SCIENCE DEGREE.ALL PATHWAY ACTIVITIES, OUTREACH EFFORTS, AND FUTURE PARTICIPATION WILL BE OPEN TO ALL QUALIFIED STUDENTS CONSISTENT WITH FEDERAL AND STATE LAW. THE PROJECT'S PRIMARY FOCUS IS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, INSTITUTIONAL COLLABORATION, AND STRENGTHENING ACADEMIC TRANSITIONS INTO FOOD SCIENCE CAREERS. THE PLANNING PHASE WILL RESULT IN A DRAFT PATHWAY FRAMEWORK, FORMALIZED PARTNER COMMITMENTS, AND AN EVALUATION STRATEGY TO MEASURE AWARENESS, TRANSFER READINESS, AND WORKFORCE PREPARATION OUTCOMES.

negativeFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE DAIRY INDUSTRY IS UNDERGOING MANY STRUCTURAL CHANGES WHICH HAS SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR ITS LONG-TERM PROFITABILITY. THIS PROJECT, I.E., INTEL, WILL BUILD CAPACITY AT THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES (DAS) OF TEXAS STATE UNIVERSITY IN OFFERING IMPROVED LEARNING EXPERIENCES TO STUDENTS BY MAKING AVAILABLE COMPUTER FACILITIES FOR STUDENTS' USE AND BY TRAINING THEM IN DATA ANALYSIS SKILLS IN COLLABORATION WITH NIMBIOS. GIVEN THE INCREASINGLY DOMINANT ROLE OF DATA ANALYSIS AND STATISTICAL MODELING IN AGRICULTURE, AND INCREASING USE OF ONLINE LEARNING, GOOD COMPUTER FACILITIES ARE BASIC INSTRUCTIONAL NEEDS IN INSTITUTIONS OFFERING AGRICULTURE-RELATED COURSES. DESPITE IMPRESSIVE NUMBERS IN STUDENT ENROLLMENT, DAS DOES NOT HAVE DEDICATED COMPUTER FACILITIES FOR STUDENTS. THEREFORE, INTEL PROPOSES TO INSTALL 30 COMPUTER SYSTEMS AND NECESSARY SOFTWARE TOOLS AT DAS. SUBSEQUENTLY, STUDENTS WILL BE OFFERED COURSES WITH MODIFIED CURRICULUM IN THE FALL AND SPRING SEMESTERS, AND SPECIALIZED TRAINING IN THE SUMMER SEMESTER. CURRICULUM MODIFICATION INVOLVES ADOPTION OF STATISTICAL ANALYSIS TOOLS AND IMPROVED CONTENT DELIVERY MECHANISMS. EXPERTS FROM NIMBIOS WILL BE AMONG RESOURCE PERSONS FOR THE SPECIAL TOPIC. DAS INTERNS WILL VISIT NIMBIOS TO LEARN ABOUT CUTTING-EDGE APPLICATIONS OF MODELING IN AGRICULTURE-RELATED SCIENCES. FINALLY, STUDENTS WILL APPLY THE TECHNIQUES THEY LEARNED DURING TRAINING INTO THE RESEARCH PROJECTS AND DEVELOP THEIR OWN THESIS UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF PROJECT DIRECTORS. INTEL WILL DEDICATE AT LEAST 50% OF AVAILABLE OPPORTUNITIES TO MINORITY STUDENTS AND FEMALE STUDENTS FOR BETTER RECRUITMENT, RETENTION AND DIVERSIFICATION.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, TIMELESSLY AND UBIQUITOUSLY, ARE CORNERSTONES IN ACHIEVING A FULFILLING AND HAPPY LIFE. WE POSIT THAT A DIFFERENT APPROACH IS NECESSARY TO ENHANCE HEALTHCARE, WHEREBY PERSONALIZED, ADAPTIVE AND INTEGRATED SMART SOLUTIONS, PAIRED WITH REAL-TIME/REAL-LIFE HEALTH/LIFESTYLE MONITORING, AID INDIVIDUALS IN MAKING INFORMED PRACTICAL HEALTH DECISIONS AND PREVENTING AND/OR MANAGING CHRONIC DISEASE. A TECHNOLOGY-BASED EMPOWERMENT DIDACTIC MODULE (TEDM) AND AN INFORMED DECISION-MAKING ENHANCER (IDME) COUPLED IN A SMART APPLICATION (APP) TAILORED FOR FARMWORKERS, TO TEACH, SET GOALS, MONITOR AND SUPPORT IN TERMS OF NUTRITION, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, CIRCADIAN RHYTHM, HYDRATION TOWARDS LOWERING T2DM AND CVD RISK, WILL BE DEVELOPED AND IMPLEMENTED CONSIDERING THE PARTICULAR CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POPULATION AND SETTING. IN PARALLEL, RIGOROUS CLINICAL ASSESSMENT WILL BE MONITORING RISK PARAMETERS FOR T2DM AND CVD AND COMPLIANCE TO DIETARY PLANS. THE APP INCORPORATING CLINICAL/BIOCHEMICAL PARAMETERS, DIETARY/LIFESTYLE BEHAVIOR AND GOAL ACHIEVEMENT DEGREE WILL BE CONSTANTLY REFINED AND IMPROVED THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING AND RE-PROGRAMMING. THE APP WILL FUNCTION AS A PROGRAMMABLE TOOL CONSTANTLY LEARNING, ADAPTING AND TAILORING ITS SERVICES TO USER,NEEDS HELPING OPTIMIZATION OF PRACTICAL INFORMED DECISION MAKING TOWARDS MINIMIZING DISEASE RISK. STUDENTS WILL BE INVOLVED IN THE PROCESS WHILE CAL POLY WILL BE ACQUIRING KNOW-HOW ON THIS TYPE OF APPROACH ALONG WITH INFRASTRUCTURE, AND STAKEHOLDERS WILL BE GAINING A HEALTHIER MORE VIBRANT WORKFORCE. THESE EFFORTS WILL WORK TOWARDS CAPACITY BUILDING AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE OUTREACH/EXTENSION ACTIVITIES COMBINED WITH EDUCATION AND RESEARCH INVOLVING STUDENTS VIA A LEARNING LAB FOR CAL POLY'S STUDENTS PRODUCING AN ACADEMIY OF HEALTH EDUCATORS COMMUNITY AMBASSADORS (AHECA) COMPRISED OF STUDENTS.

THE PROJECT WILL BUILD LASTING RELATIONSHIPS WITH THREE REGIONAL HISPANIC-SERVING COMMUNITY COLLEGES, LUNA COMMUNITY COLLEGE (LCC), SANTA FE COMMUNITY COLLEGE (SFCC) AND THE COMMUNITY COLLEGE OF DENVER (CCD) THAT SUPPORT THE TRANSFER OF NATURAL RESOURCE STUDENTS BY INCORPORATING CROSS-INSTITUTIONAL PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR ALL PARTICIPATING FACULTY WITH A TEAM-TEACHING MODEL THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT.

THE RAPID DEVELOPMENT OF REMOTE SENSING SERVICES DEMONSTRATES THE CRITICAL NEED OF THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY FOR THESE TECHNOLOGIES; HOWEVER, BOTH FUNDAMENTAL AND APPLIED SCIENCE ARE NEEDED TO DEVELOP APPLICATIONS THAT CAN ADDRESS REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS AT SCALE. OUR HOPE IS THAT THIS EQUIPMENT WOULD ALSO SERVE AS THE BASIS FOR A JOINT CENTER ON DATA ASSIMILATION FOR SPATIAL ANALYSIS OF SOILS AND CROP PERFORMANCE IN COLLABORATION WITH SCIENTISTS FROM NEIGHBORING UNIVERSITIES.

MEETING THE INCREASING DEMAND FOR AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES FOR FOOD, FEED, FUEL AND OTHER USES, WITHOUT PUTTING GREATER PRESSURE ON THE WORLD'S NATURAL RESOURCES, WILL REQUIRE INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS GENERATED BY THE NEXT GENERATION OF DIVERSE AND WELL-TRAINED SCIENTISTS IN FOOD, AGRICULTURAL, NATURAL RESOURCES AND HUMAN (FANH) SCIENCES. DESPITE THIS GROWING DEMAND FOR A SKILLED WORKFORCE, UNDERGRADUATE STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION REMAIN MAJOR CHALLENGES FOR INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION, AS WELL AS FOR THE AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD INDUSTRY. THESE CHALLENGES ARE EXACERBATED FOR LOW-INCOME, FIRST-GENERATION, AND TRADITIONALLY UNDERREPRESENTED MINORITY (URM) STUDENTS WHO GENERALLY LACK STRONG NETWORKS AND CONNECTIONS TO FACULTY AND MENTORS THAT WOULD INCREASE THEIR SUCCESS, PARTICULARLY IN STEM COURSES AND RESEARCH EXPERIENCES. HERE, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A PROGRAM TO ENHANCE CURRENT PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN CALIFORNIA STATE UNIVERSITY MONTEREY BAY (CSUMB) AND HARTNELL COLLEGE (HC), TWO HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTIONS LOCATED IN MONTEREY COUNTY, CALIFORNIA, AN AREA POPULARLY REFERRED AS THE SALAD BOWL OF THE WORLD, AND EQUALLY KNOWN FOR HAVING ONE OF THE WIDEST INCOME DISPARITIES BETWEEN HISPANIC AND WHITE POPULATIONS. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROGRAM IS TO ADVANCE EDUCATIONAL ACHIEVEMENT AND ENTHUSIASM FOR FANH FIELDS, PROMOTING THE TRANSFER PROCESS FROM HC TO CSUMB, AND TO IMPROVE SOCIAL MOBILITY BY PREPARING REGIONAL STUDENTS FOR CAREERS IN THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO IMPROVE STUDENT-LEARNING THROUGH THE IMPLEMENTATION OF COURSE-BASED UNDERGRADUATE RESEARCH EXPERIENCES IN THE CLASSROOM, AIMED AT ENHANCING PROFESSIONAL AND ACADEMIC GROWTH OF PARTICIPATING STUDENTS, AS WELL AS THEIR ABILITY TO IDENTIFY THEMSELVES AS POTENTIAL ACTIVE PARTICIPANT OF THE SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH COMMUNITY WORKING TO ADDRESS THE CHALLENGES EXPERIENCED BY THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY. THESE COURSE-BASED RESEARCH EXPERIENCES WILL ALSO ENHANCE EARLY PARTICIPATION AND EXPOSURETO INTERDISCIPLINARY LABORATORY AND FIELD-BASED RESEARCH OFFERING AUTHENTIC EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR COMMUNITY COLLEGE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS TO IMPROVE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH AND MODERN MICROBIAL BIOTECHNOLOGY RESEARCH APPROACHES, INCLUDING MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTICS OF SOILBORNE PATHOGENS, AS WELL AS UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPLEX ISSUES SURROUNDING PLANT DISEASE MANAGEMENT. COLLECTIVELY, THESE EFFORTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO EMPOWER URM STUDENTS AT HISPANIC SERVING INSTITUTIONS TO BECOME THE NEXT GENERATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROFESSIONALS THAT WILL FILL THE LARGE AND GROWING NUMBER OF AGRICULTURAL JOBS IN OUR REGION AND STATE. PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES AND THE ORGANIZATION OF A REGIONAL CAREER FAIR WILL ALLOW STUDENTS FROM THE TRI-COUNTY REGION TO MEET WITH PRIVATE ORGANIZATIONS AND FEDERAL AGENCIES TO EXPLORE CAREERS AND PROFESSIONAL RESOURCES, AND TO BECOME AWARE OF RELEVANT JOB OPENINGS, INTERNSHIPS, AND SCHOLARSHIPS. ULTIMATELY, THE MISSION-ORIENTED RESEARCH PROPOSED IN THIS PROJECT FOCUSING ON CHARACTERIZING INDIGENOUSSOIL BACTERIAL POPULATIONS FROM ADAPTED TO LOCAL AGRICULTURAL ENVIRONMENTS AND CATALOGUING THEIR ANTIMICROBIAL CAPACITIES AND BIOCONTROL POTENTIAL AGAINST PLANT PATHOGENS OF LOCALLY-GROWN CROPS IS AIMED AT ADDRESSING REAL-WORLD PROBLEMS, AND SPECIFICALLY, TO ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING OF THE DIVERSITY AND FUNCTION OF INDIGENOUS SOIL MICROBIAL COMMUNITIES, AND THEIR POTENTIAL APPLICATIONS TO PROMOTE SOIL HEALTH AND AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY.

**AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** DAIRY FARMS ARE INCREASINGLY BECOMING MORE CONSOLIDATED, WHILE SMALL FAMILY FARMS ARE RAPIDLY DECLINING. EACH YEAR WISCONSIN LOSES SEVERAL HUNDRED FAMILY FARMS. THESE CHANGES UNDOUBTABLY HAVE AN IMPACT ON THE SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC CONDITIONS IN RURAL COMMUNITIES, AFFECTING SOCIAL AND MENTAL WELL-BEING OF INDIVIDUALS. FOR EXAMPLE, CONCERNS ABOUT MENTAL HEALTH AND INCREASED SUICIDE OCCURRENCE FROM AGRICULTURAL AND RURAL COMMUNITIES HAVE BEEN REPORTED. WITH A NEED TO INCREASE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION BY 50% UNTIL THE YEAR 2050, WE NEED TO ENSURE OUR PRODUCTION SYSTEMS ARE RESILIENT IN ALL ASPECTS OF THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC SYSTEM, REQUIRING MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACHES THAT ADDRESS WHICH FACTORS CONTRIBUTE TO RESILIENT ECOSYSTEMS, GREATER COMMUNITY WELFARE, INCLUDING MENTAL HEALTH, AS WELL AS IMPROVED ANIMAL WELFARE, AND THUS ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY. IF WE RECOGNIZE THAT SUSTAINABILITY IS MORE THAN JUST PROTECTING THE ENVIRONMENT, WE CAN RECOGNIZE THAT FOSTERING SUSTAINABILITY IN THE DAIRY INDUSTRY MEANS ENSURING ECONOMIC VIABILITY FOR DAIRY FARMERS, AS WELL AS MENTAL AND PHYSICAL WELL-BEING. GIVEN THE SENSITIVITY AROUND MANY OF THESE ISSUES, ESTABLISHING GOOD RELATIONSHIPS WITH FARMERS IS VITAL.SUPPORT FROM THIS GRANT ALLOWS FOR FOUNDATIONAL OUTREACH TO ESTABLISH CONTACTS AND BUILD TRUST BETWEEN FARMERS AND RESEARCHERS, ALLOWING FOR MORE ROBUST AND HONEST DISCUSSIONS AND SHARING OF INFORMATION. negativeFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** METHANE HAS NEGATIVE EFFECTS ON THE CLIMATE DUE TO ITS HIGH GLOBAL WARMING POTENTIAL. HUMAN ACTIVITIES SUCH AS AGRICULTURE, WASTE DISPOSAL AND FOSSIL FUEL PRODUCTION PRODUCE ABOUT 60% OF THE WORLD'S METHANE EMISSIONS THAT IS RESPONSIBLE FOR AT LEAST 25% OF TODAY'S GLOBAL WARMING. ENTERIC FERMENTATION AND MANURE MANAGEMENT ARE THE TWO PROCESSES PRODUCING METHANE IN LIVESTOCK. WASTING PART OF THE FEED ENERGY IN THE FORM OF METHANE IS NOT ONLY A CLIMATE ISSUE BUT ALSO A PRODUCTION PROBLEM. ACCORDING TO THE UNITED NATIONS, THE WORLD POPULATION IS ABOUT 7.7 BILLION IN 2019 AND EXPECTED TO GROW TO AROUND 8.5, 9.7 AND 10.9 BILLION IN 2030, 2050 AND 2100, RESPECTIVELY. THIS POPULATION GROWTH IS THE MAIN MOTIVATION OF THE INCREASED DEMAND FOR LIVESTOCK PRODUCTS. TO MEET THE GROWING GLOBAL DEMANDS OVER THE NEXT 50 YEARS, IT IS ESTIMATED THAT LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SHOULD INCREASE BY 70%. THEREFORE, METHANE EMISSIONS ARE EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO INCREASE AS THE DEMAND FOR ANIMAL PRODUCTS INCREASES. THEREFORE, SCIENTISTS HAVE BEEN INVESTIGATING DIFFERENT STRATEGIES TO REDUCE METHANE EMISSIONS AS COMMUNITIES BECAME MORE AWARE OF THE NEGATIVE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON THE ENVIRONMENT. MEASURING METHANE EMISSION ON A LARGE-SCALE LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION FARM IS CHALLENGING DUE TO THE HIGH COSTS AND THE LOW THROUGHPUT OF THE TRADITIONAL USED METHODS. THIS PROJECT WILL CONDUCT A NUMBER OF EXPERIMENTS IN THE LAB AND FIELD TO DEVELOP A LOW COST AND A HIGHLY EFFICIENT SYSTEM THAT WILL BE ABLE TO MONITOR AND MEASURE METHANE EMISSION ON A LARGER SCALE USING COMPUTER VISION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNIQUES. THE RESULTS OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE USED FOR PROMOTING GREENER LIVESTOCK AND DISSEMINATED IN A STRAIGHTFORWARD WAY TO LIVESTOCK PRODUCERSTHROUGH CONDUCTING WORKSHOPS AND ACCESSIBLE WEBSITE. THIS PROJECT WILL CONDUCT EDUCATION WORKSHOPS TO ANIMAL SCIENCE STUDENTS TO ENRICH THEIR SKILLS IN USING AI TECHNOLOGIES IN THE FIELD OF ANIMAL SCIENCE. IN CONCLUSION, THE EXPECTED OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE USED BY LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS FOR BETTER MANAGEMENT PRACTICES SUCH AS CHOOSING THE OPTIMAL DIET FOR THEIR HERD AND MANURE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT WILL HELP WITH REDUCING METHANE EMISSION.
